52Kaccāyana Sutta. 60Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Jinavacanayuttaṃ hi
[Jinavacanayuttaṃ + hi = 2 words]

“Jinavacanayuttaṃ hi” icc etaṃ adhikāratthaṃ veditabbaṃ.

Conforming to the Word of the Victorious One.
“Conforming to the Word of the Victorious One (Buddha)”. This should be understood as a governing aphorism,1This is an adhikāra-sutta, a governing aphorism of general application that rules the whole work. There are three kinds of adhikāra: (1) sīha-gatika (“lion's movement”), which affects all the preceding and following suttas; (2) maṇḍūka-gatika (“frog's movement”), which affects only certain suttas related to one another; and (3) yathānupubbika, which affects in sequential order, especially the following suttas. The present sutta is of the first kind. Everything mentioned in this text is in accordance with the word of the Buddha, that is, with the language used by him. i.e., as applying to all the suttas backward and forward.
1This is an adhikāra-sutta, a governing aphorism of general application that rules the whole work. There are three kinds of adhikāra: (1) sīha-gatika (“lion's movement”), which affects all the preceding and following suttas; (2) maṇḍūka-gatika (“frog's movement”), which affects only certain suttas related to one another; and (3) yathānupubbika, which affects in sequential order, especially the following suttas. The present sutta is of the first kind. Everything mentioned in this text is in accordance with the word of the Buddha, that is, with the language used by him.

53Kaccāyana Sutta. 61Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Liṅgañ ca nippajjate (192)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Liṅgaṃ + ca + nippajjate = 3 words]

Yathā yatthā jinavacanayuttaṃ hi liṅgaṃ, tathā tathā idha liṅgañ ca nippajjate.

Taṃ yathā? Eso no satthā, brahmā, attā, sakhā, rājā.

And the base should be established.2The particle “ca” in the sutta serves to include the roots (dhātu) as well; these too should be established in conformity with the Word of the Victorious One. The term liṅga can be translated in this context as “base” or “stem”; in other grammatical contexts it means gender. The real examples of this sutta are the bases “esa”, “amha”, “satthu”, “brahma”, “atta”, “sakha” and “rāja”; since it is impossible to show the bases without their inflections (nāma-vibhatti), they are presented here as completed words –base plus inflection–.
Here the base should be established in such a way that it conforms to the Word of the Victorious One.
As what? Eso no Satthā (this is our Teacher), brahmā (Brahmā), attā (the self; oneself), sakhā (friend), rājā (king).
2The particle “ca” in the sutta serves to include the roots (dhātu) as well; these too should be established in conformity with the Word of the Victorious One. [Tato + ca + vibhattiyo = 3 words]

Tato jinavacanayuttehi liṅgehi vibhattiyo parā honti.

And after those, the [nominal] inflections.3The particle “ca” in the sutta indicates that the inflections are also employed after the indeclinables that end with the suffixes ‘tave’, ‘tunā’, etc.
Inflections are placed after the bases that conform to the Word of the Victorious One.

55Kaccāyana Sutta. 63Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Si yo, aṃ yo, nā hi, sa naṃ, smā hi, sa naṃ, smiṃ su (200)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Si yo, aṃ yo, nā hi, sa naṃ, smā hi, sa naṃ, smiṃ su = 1 word]

Kā ca pana tāyo vibhattiyo? Si, yo iti paṭhamā; aṃ, yo iti dutiyā; nā, hi iti tatiyā; sa, naṃ iti catutthī; smā, hi iti pañcamī; sa, naṃ iti chaṭṭhī; smiṃ, su iti sattamī.

Vibhatti icc anena kvattho? Amhassa mamaṃ savibhattissa se.

‘Si, yo’, ‘aṃ, yo’, ‘nā, hi’, ‘sa, naṃ’, ‘smā, hi’, ‘sa, naṃ’, ‘smiṃ, su’.4The inflections are divided into eight pairs: first (paṭhamā), second (dutiyā), third (tatiyā), fourth (catutthī), fifth (pañcamī), sixth (chaṭṭhī), seventh (sattamī) and eighth (aṭṭhamī). Aṭṭhamī is the name of the endings of the vocative case and, in the order of the declensions, it is placed after the first. The first of each pair is singular and the second is plural. Pāḷi has no dual number.
And which are those inflections? ‘Si, yo’ are the first [pair]; ‘aṃ, yo’ the second; ‘nā, hi’ the third; ‘sa, naṃ’ the fourth; ‘smā, hi’ the fifth; ‘sa, naṃ’ the sixth; ‘smiṃ, su’ the seventh.
What is the use of saying “inflection”? [To use it in suttas such as] “Amhassa mamaṃ savibhattissa se” (§120), etc. When ‘sa’ follows, “amha” together with the inflection [is substituted by] “mamaṃ”.
4The inflections are divided into eight pairs: first (paṭhamā), second (dutiyā), third (tatiyā), fourth (catutthī), fifth (pañcamī), sixth (chaṭṭhī), seventh (sattamī) and eighth (aṭṭhamī). Aṭṭhamī is the name of the endings of the vocative case and, in the order of the declensions, it is placed after the first. The first of each pair is singular and the second is plural. Pāḷi has no dual number.

56Kaccāyana Sutta. 64Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Tadanuparodhena
[Taṃ-an-uparodhena = 1 word]

Yathā yathā tesaṃ jinavacanānaṃ anuparodho, tathā tathā idha liṅgañ ca nippajjate.

By not contradicting those.5The particle “ca” in the sutta indicates that the verbs (ākhyāta) should also be formed in conformity with the Word of the Victorious One. The difference between this sutta and §53 · Liṅgañ ca nippajjate — And the base should be established.">§53 is that by §53 · Liṅgañ ca nippajjate — And the base should be established.">§53 the base should be established in conformity with the Word of the Victorious One, while by this sutta the completed form should be established in conformity with the Word of the Victorious One. Example: according to §53 · Liṅgañ ca nippajjate — And the base should be established.">§53, the base of the word “puriso” (nominative singular) should be put down as “purisa” and not as “puruṣa” (as in Sanskrit); when the word is formed, it should be “puriso” and not “puruṣaḥ”.
Here the gender [and the completed form] should be established in such a way that it does not contradict the Words of the Victorious One.
5The particle “ca” in the sutta indicates that the verbs (ākhyāta) should also be formed in conformity with the Word of the Victorious One. The difference between this sutta and §53 is that by §53 the base should be established in conformity with the Word of the Victorious One, while by this sutta the completed form should be established in conformity with the Word of the Victorious One. Example: according to §53, the base of the word “puriso” (nominative singular) should be put down as “purisa” and not as “puruṣa” (as in Sanskrit); when the word is formed, it should be “puriso” and not “puruṣaḥ”.

57Kaccāyana Sutta. 71Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Ālapane si gasañño (204)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Ālapane + si + gasañño = 3 words]

Ālapanatthe si gasañño hoti.

Bhoti ayye (Vin. ii, 280)Vinaya-piṭaka · vol. ii, p. 280; bhoti kaññe; bhoti Kharādiye (Khu. v, 4)Khuddaka-nikāya · vol. v, p. 4.

Ālapane ti kimatthaṃ? Sā ayyā (Vin. ii, 307)Vinaya-piṭaka · vol. ii, p. 307.

Sī ti kimatthaṃ? Bhotiyo ayyāyo (Vin. ii, 288)Vinaya-piṭaka · vol. ii, p. 288.

Ga icc anena kvattho? Ghat’ e ca.

In the vocative, ‘si’ is named ‘ga’.
In the meaning of vocative, ‘si’ has the name ‘ga’.
Examples
  1. Bhoti ayye = Dear lady!6Both “bhoti” and “ayye”, etc., are examples. When forming these words, the inflection ‘si’ is employed; then, by this sutta, ‘si’ is named ‘ga’, and the application of the other suttas follows to complete the word.
  2. Bhoti kaññe = Dear girl!
  3. Bhoti Kharādiye = Dear Kharādiyā!

What is the purpose of saying “vocative”? [To prevent the operation of this rule in other cases such as] “Sā ayyā” (that lady) –here the case is not vocative but nominative–.

What is the purpose of saying ‘si’? [To prevent the operation of this rule in the example] “Bhotiyo ayyāyo” –here the inflection is ‘yo’, not ‘si’–.7There are two inflections ‘si’: (1) the ‘si’ of the nominative singular (paṭhamā) and (2) the ‘si’ of the vocative singular (ālapana), to which this sutta gives the name ‘ga’. The purpose of this name is to allow the application of the morphological procedures prescribed by the pertinent suttas, and to distinguish precisely between both inflections ‘si’. This explanation was taken from the book of the Venerable A. Thitzana.

What is the use of the name ‘ga’? [For the use of the name ‘ga’ in suttas such as] “Ghat’ e ca” (§114). After ‘gha’ there is [substitution of ‘ga’] by ‘e’.8Both “bhoti” and “ayye”, etc., are examples. When forming these words, the inflection ‘si’ is employed; then, by this sutta, ‘si’ is named ‘ga’, and the application of the other suttas follows to complete the word.

58Kaccāyana Sutta. 29Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Ivaṇṇ’-uvaṇṇā jha-lā (205)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Ivaṇṇa-uvaṇṇā + jha-lā = 2 words]

Ivaṇṇ’-uvaṇṇā icc ete jha-lasaññā honti yathāsaṅkhyaṃ.

Isino, aggino, gahapatino, daṇḍino. Setuno, ketuno, bhikkhuno. Sayambhuno, abhibhuno.

Jha la icc anena kvattho? Jha-lato sassa no vā.

‘I’, ‘ī’ and ‘u’, ‘ū’ [are named] ‘jha’, ‘la’.
The letters ‘i’ and ‘ī’, and ‘u’ and ‘ū’, are respectively named ‘jha’ and ‘la’.
The examples are “isino”, etc. When forming the word “isino”, first the base is put down as “isi”, then the sixth inflection ‘sa’ is employed; then the second ‘i’ of “isi” is given the name ‘jha’ by this sutta. The same should be done with the nouns whose bases end in ‘ī’, ‘u’, ‘ū’.
What is the use of the names ‘jha’ and ‘la’? [For the use of the names ‘jha’ and ‘la’ in suttas such as] “Jha-lato sassa no vā” (§117). Optionally, after ‘jha’ and ‘la’, ‘sa’ [is substituted by ‘no’].
Studied
59Kaccāyana Sutta. 182Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Te itthikhyā po (206)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Te + itthikhyā + po = 3 words]

Te ivaṇṇ’-uvaṇṇā yadā itthikhyā, tadā pasaññā honti.

Rattiyā, itthiyā, dhenuyā, vadhuyā.

Itthikhyā ti kimatthaṃ? Isinā, bhikkhunā.

Pa icc anena kvattho? Pato yā.

Those that mean feminine [gender] [are named] ‘pa’.
Those letters ‘i’, ‘ī’ and ‘u’, ‘ū’, when they mean feminine [gender], are named ‘pa’.
Examples: rattiyā (by night), itthiyā (by the woman), dhenuyā (by the cow), vadhuyā (by the daughter-in-law).9When forming “rattiyā” (by night), first the base “ratti” is put down, then the inflection ‘nā’ is employed. Then, by this sutta, ‘i’ of the feminine form “ratti” is named ‘pa’. Then the suttas “Pato yā”, etc., are applied.
What is the purpose of saying “mean feminine [gender]”? [To prevent the operation of this rule in examples such as] “isinā” (by the sage), “bhikkhunā” (by the bhikkhu) – [these are not named ‘pa’ since they are masculine].
What is the use of the name ‘pa’? [For the use of the name ‘pa’ in suttas such as] “Pato yā” (§112). After ‘pa’, [‘nā’, etc., are substituted by] ‘ya’.
9When forming “rattiyā” (by night), first the base “ratti” is put down, then the inflection ‘nā’ is employed. Then, by this sutta, ‘i’ of the feminine form “ratti” is named ‘pa’. Then the suttas “Pato yā”, etc., are applied.

60Kaccāyana Sutta. 177Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Ā gho (207)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Ā + gho = 2 words]

Ākāro yadā itthikhyo, tadā ghasañño hoti.

Saddhāya, kaññāya, vīṇāya, gaṅgāya, disāya, sālāya, mālāya, tulāya, dolāya, pabhāya, sobhāya, paññāya, karuṇāya, nāvāya, kapālikāya.

Ā ti kimatthaṃ? Rattiyā, itthiyā.

Itthikhyo ti kimatthaṃ? Satthārā desito ayaṃ dhammo.

Gha icc anena kvattho? Ghato nādīnaṃ.

‘Ā’ [is named] ‘gha’.
The letter ‘ā’, when it means feminine [gender], is named ‘gha’.
Examples: saddhāya (by/with confidence), kaññāya (by/with the girl), vīṇāya (by/with the lute), gaṅgāya (by/with the river Ganges), disāya (by/with the direction), sālāya (by/with the hall), mālāya (by/with the garland), tulāya (by/with the scale), dolāya (by the cradle), pabhāya (by/with the light), sobhāya (by/with the beauty), paññāya (by/with wisdom), karuṇāya (by/with compassion), nāvāya (by/with the boat), kapālikāya (by/with the small bowl).
When forming “saddhāya” (by/with confidence), etc., the base is put down as “saddhā”, etc. The inflection ‘nā’ is employed; then the ‘ā’ of “saddhā”, etc., is named ‘gha’, and the application of the other suttas follows.
What is the purpose of saying ‘ā’? [There is no application of this sutta in] “rattiyā”, “itthiyā” [because in these cases the letter is ‘i’ or ‘ī’, not ‘ā’].
What is the purpose of saying “means feminine [gender]”? [In the example] “Satthārā desito ayaṃ dhammo” (this Dhamma taught by the Teacher) [there is no application of this sutta because the word is masculine].
What is the use of the name ‘gha’? [For the use of the name ‘gha’ in suttas such as] “Ghato nādīnaṃ” (§111). After ‘ga’, [there is substitution by ‘āya’] of those [singular inflections] beginning with ‘nā’, etc.
Studied
61Kaccāyana Sutta. 86Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Sāgamo se (208)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Sa-āgamo + se = 2 words]

Sakārāgamo hoti se vibhattimhi.

Purisassa, aggissa, isissa, daṇḍissa, bhikkhussa, sayambhussa, abhibhussa.

Se ti kimatthaṃ? Purisasmiṃ.

When ‘sa’ [follows], [there is] insertion of ‘s’.
When the inflection ‘sa’ follows, there is insertion of ‘s’.
Example: purisassa = purisa + sa. By this sutta ‘s’ is inserted after the base. The rest are to be understood similarly.
What is the purpose of saying ‘se’? [There is no application of this sutta in the example] “purisasmiṃ” (in the man), [since the inflection is not ‘sa’ but ‘smiṃ’].
Studied
62Kaccāyana Sutta. 206Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Saṃ-sāsv ekavacanesu ca (209)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Saṃ-sāsu + ekavacanesu + ca = 3 words]

Saṃ-sāsu ekavacanesu vibhattādesesu sakārāgamo hoti.

Etissaṃ, etissā; imissaṃ, imissā; tissaṃ, tissā; tassaṃ, tassā; yassaṃ, yassā; amussaṃ, amussā.

Saṃ-sāsv iti kimatthaṃ? Agginā, pāṇinā.

Ekavacanesv iti kimatthaṃ? Tāsaṃ, sabbāsaṃ.

Vibhattādesesv iti kimatthaṃ? Manasā, vacasā, thāmasā.

And when the singular ‘saṃ’ and ‘sā’ [follow].
When ‘saṃ’ and ‘sā’, which are substitutions of the singular inflections [‘smiṃ’ and ‘sa’], follow, there is insertion of ‘s’.10‘Saṃ’ and ‘sā’ are substitutions of the inflections ‘smiṃ’ and ‘sa’ respectively, after pronouns named ‘gha’ and ‘pa’ (see §179 · Gha-pato smiṃ-sānaṃ saṃ-sā — ‘Saṃ’ and ‘sā’ of ‘smiṃ’ and ‘sa’ after ‘gha’ and ‘pa’.">§179). This sutta prescribes the additional insertion of ‘s’ before those substitutions.
Examples
  1. Etissaṃ = etā + smiṃ (‘ā’ of “etā” is substituted by ‘i’ (§63); ‘smiṃ’ is substituted by ‘saṃ’ (§179) and ‘s’ is inserted (§62)). Meaning: “in that”. [Feminine gender.]
  2. Etissā = etā + sa (‘ā’ of “etā” is substituted by ‘i’ (§63); ‘sa’ is substituted by ‘sā’ (§179) and ‘s’ is inserted (§62)). Meaning: “of that”. [Feminine gender.]
  3. The rest (imissaṃ, imissā; tissaṃ, tissā; tassaṃ, tassā; yassaṃ, yassā; amussaṃ, amussā) are to be understood similarly.

What is the purpose of saying “‘saṃ’ and ‘sā’”? [This sutta does not apply when there is no ‘saṃ’ or ‘sā’, such as in] “agginā” (with fire) and “pāṇinā” (with the hand).

What is the purpose of saying “singular”? [This sutta does not apply when the words are not singular, such as in] tāsaṃ (of those) and sabbāsaṃ (of all).

What is the purpose of saying “which are substitutions of inflections”? [This sutta does not apply when there are no substitutions of inflections, such as in] manasā (with the mind), vacasā (with speech) and thāmasā (with strength).

10‘Saṃ’ and ‘sā’ are substitutions of the inflections ‘smiṃ’ and ‘sa’ respectively, after pronouns named ‘gha’ and ‘pa’ (see §179). This sutta prescribes the additional insertion of ‘s’ before those substitutions.
Studied
63Kaccāyana Sutta. 217Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Et’-imāsam i (210)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Etā-imāsaṃ + i = 2 words]

Etā-imā icc etesam anto saro ikāro hoti saṃ-sāsu ekavacanesu vibhattādesesu.

Etissaṃ, etissā; imissaṃ, imissā.

Saṃ-sāsv iti kimatthaṃ? Etāya, imāya.

Ekavacanesv iti kimatthaṃ? Etāsaṃ, imāsaṃ.

‘I’ of “etā” and “imā”.
When ‘saṃ’ and ‘sā’, which are substitutions of the singular inflections [‘smiṃ’ and ‘sa’], follow, the end vowel ‘ā’ of “etā” and “imā” is substituted by ‘i’.
Examples: the same as the previous sutta.
What is the purpose of saying “‘saṃ’ and ‘sā’”? [This sutta does not apply when there is no ‘saṃ’ or ‘sā’, such as in] etāya and imāya.
What is the purpose of saying “singular”? [This sutta does not apply when the words are not singular, such as in] etāsaṃ and imāsaṃ.

64Kaccāyana Sutta. 216Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Tassā vā (211)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Tassā + vā = 2 words]

Tassā itthiyaṃ vattamānāya ākārassa ikāro hoti vā saṃ-sāsu ekavacanesu vibhattādesesu.

Tissaṃ, tissā; tassaṃ, tassā.

Optionally, [‘ā’] of “tā”.
Optionally, when ‘saṃ’ and ‘sā’, which are substitutions of the singular inflections [‘smiṃ’ and ‘sa’], follow, the [end vowel] ‘ā’ of “tā”, in the feminine [gender], is substituted by ‘i’.
Examples
  1. Tissaṃ = tā + smiṃ (‘smiṃ’ is substituted by ‘saṃ’ (§179); ‘ā’ of “tā” is substituted by ‘i’ (§64) and ‘s’ is inserted (§62)).
  2. Tissā = tā + sa (‘sa’ is substituted by ‘sā’ (§179); ‘ā’ of “tā” is substituted by ‘i’ (§64) and ‘s’ is inserted (§62)).
Studied
65Kaccāyana Sutta. 215Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Tato sassa ssāya (212)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Tato + sassa + ssāya = 3 words]

Tato tā-etā-imāto sassa vibhattissa ssāyādeso hoti vā.

Tissāya, etissāya, imissāya.

Vā ti kimatthaṃ? Tissā, etissā, imissā.

After ‘tā’, ‘ssāya’ of ‘sa’.
Optionally, after “tā”, “etā” and “imā”, the inflection ‘sa’ is substituted by ‘ssāya’.
Examples
  1. Tissāya = tā + sa (‘ā’ of “tā” is substituted by ‘i’ (§64); ‘sa’ is substituted by ‘ssāya’ (§65)).
  2. Etissāya = etā + sa (‘ā’ of “etā” is substituted by ‘i’ (§63); ‘sa’ is substituted by ‘ssāya’ (§65)).
  3. Imissāya = imā + sa (‘ā’ of “imā” is substituted by ‘i’ (§63); ‘sa’ is substituted by ‘ssāya’ (§65)).

What is the purpose of saying “optionally”? [In the following examples ‘sa’ is not substituted by ‘ssāya’:] tissā, etissā, imissā.

Studied
66Kaccāyana Sutta. 205Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Gho rassaṃ (213)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Gho + rassaṃ = 2 words]

Gho rassam āpajjate saṃ-sāsu ekavacanesu vibhattādesesu.

Tassaṃ, tassā; yassaṃ, yassā; sabbassaṃ, sabbassā.

Saṃ-sāsv iti kimatthaṃ? Tāya, sabbāya.

Ekavacanesv iti kimatthaṃ? Tāsaṃ, sabbāsaṃ.

‘Gha’ [becomes short].
When ‘saṃ’ and ‘sā’, which are substitutions of the singular inflections [‘smiṃ’ and ‘sa’], follow, ‘gha’ becomes short.
Examples
  1. Tassaṃ = tā + smiṃ (‘smiṃ’ is substituted by ‘saṃ’ (§179); ‘s’ is inserted (§62); ‘ā’ is named ‘gha’ (§60); ‘ā’ of “tā” is shortened (§66)).
  2. Tassā = tā + sa (‘s’ is inserted (§62); ‘ā’ is named ‘gha’ (§60); ‘ā’ of “tā” is shortened (§66))
  3. Yassaṃ = yā + smiṃ (‘smiṃ’ is substituted by ‘saṃ’ (§179); ‘s’ is inserted (§62); ‘ā’ is named ‘gha’ (§60); ‘ā’ of “yā” is shortened (§66)).
  4. Yassā = yā + sa (‘s’ is inserted (§62); ‘ā’ is named ‘gha’ (§60); ‘ā’ of “yā” is shortened (§66))
  5. Sabbassaṃ = sabbā + smiṃ (‘smiṃ’ is substituted by ‘saṃ’ (§179); ‘s’ is inserted (§62); ‘ā’ is named ‘gha’ (§60); ‘ā’ of “sabbā” is shortened (§66)).
  6. Sabbassā = sabbā + sa (‘s’ is inserted (§62); ‘ā’ is named ‘gha’ (§60); ‘ā’ of “sabbā” is shortened (§66))

What is the purpose of saying “‘saṃ’ and ‘sā’”? [This sutta does not apply when there is no ‘saṃ’ or ‘sā’, such as in] tāya, sabbāya.

What is the purpose of saying “singular”? [This sutta does not apply when the words are not singular, such as in] tāsaṃ, sabbāsaṃ.

Studied
67Kaccāyana Sutta. 229Rūpasiddhi Sutta.No ca dvādito naṃmhi (214)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[No + ca + dvi-ādito + naṃmhi = 4 words]

Dvi icc evamādito saṅkhyāto nakārāgamo hoti naṃmhi vibhattimhi.

Dvinnaṃ, tinnaṃ, catunnaṃ, pañcannaṃ, channaṃ, sattannaṃ, aṭṭhannaṃ, navannaṃ, dasannaṃ.

Dvādito ti kimatthaṃ? Sahassānaṃ.

Naṃmhi ti kimatthaṃ? Dvīsu, tīsu.

Caggahaṇena ssañ c’ āgamo hoti. Catassannaṃ itthīnaṃ; tissannaṃ vedanānaṃ.

And when ‘naṃ’ [follows], after “dvi” and others, [there is insertion of] ‘n’.
After the numerals “dvi” (two) and others, the letter ‘n’ is inserted when the inflection ‘naṃ’ follows.
Examples
  1. Dvinnaṃ (of two) = dvi + naṃ (by this sutta ‘n’ is inserted).
  2. Tinnaṃ (of three), catunnaṃ (of four), pañcannaṃ (of five), channaṃ (of six), sattannaṃ (of seven), aṭṭhannaṃ (of eight), navannaṃ (of nine), dasannaṃ (of ten). The formation of these numerals is similar to the previous one.

What is the purpose of saying “‘dvi’ and others”? [This sutta does not apply to higher numbers such as] sahassānaṃ (of thousands).

What is the purpose of saying “when ‘naṃ’ follows”? [This sutta does not apply when ‘naṃ’ does not follow, such as in] dvīsu (in two), tīsu (in three).

And by taking “ca”, ‘ssa’ is also inserted.

Examples
  1. Catassannaṃ = catu + naṃ (‘u’ of “catu” is substituted by ‘a’ (§404); by “ca” of this sutta ‘ssa’ is inserted). Catassannaṃ itthīnaṃ (of four women).
  2. Tissannaṃ = ti + naṃ (by “ca” of this sutta ‘ssa’ is inserted). Tissannaṃ vedanānaṃ (of three feelings).

68Kaccāyana Sutta. 184Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Am-ā pato smiṃ-smānaṃ vā (216)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Aṃ-ā + pato + smiṃ-smānaṃ + vā = 4 words]

Pa icc etasmā smiṃ smā icc etesaṃ aṃ-ā ādesā honti vā yathāsaṅkhyaṃ.

Matyaṃ, matiyaṃ, matyā (Khu. vi, 39)Khuddaka-nikāya · vol. vi, p. 39, matiyā. Nikatyaṃ, nikatiyaṃ (Khu. vi, 39)Khuddaka-nikāya · vol. vi, p. 39, nikatyā (Khu. v, 9)Khuddaka-nikāya · vol. v, p. 9, nikatiyā. Vikatyaṃ, vikatiyaṃ, vikatyā, vikatiyā. Viratyaṃ, viratiyaṃ, viratyā, viratiyā. Ratyaṃ, ratiyaṃ, ratyā (Khu. vi, 315)Khuddaka-nikāya · vol. vi, p. 315, ratiyā. Puthabyaṃ, puthaviyaṃ, puthabyā, puthaviyā. Pavatyaṃ, pavatyā, pavattiyaṃ, pavattiyā.

Optionally, after ‘pa’, ‘aṃ’ and ‘ā’ of ‘smiṃ’ and ‘smā’.
Optionally, after ‘pa’, ‘smiṃ’ and ‘smā’ are substituted by ‘aṃ’ and ‘ā’ respectively.
Examples
  1. Matyaṃ = mati + smiṃ (‘i’ of “mati” is named ‘pa’ (§59); ‘smiṃ’ is substituted by ‘aṃ’ (§68); ‘i’ of “mati” is substituted by ‘y’ (§72)).
  2. Matyā = mati + smā (‘i’ of “mati” is named ‘pa’ (§59); ‘smā’ is substituted by ‘ā’ (§68); ‘i’ of “mati” is substituted by ‘y’ (§72)).
  3. The formation of the rest of the examples is similar to the previous ones.

69Kaccāyana Sutta. 186Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Ādito o ca (218)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Ādito + o + ca = 3 words]

Ādi icc etasmā smiṃ-vacanassa aṃ-o ādesā honti vā.

Ādiṃ, ādo.

Vā ti kimatthaṃ? Ādismiṃ, ādimhi nāthaṃ namassitvāna.

Caggahaṇena aññasmā pi smiṃvacanassa ā-o-aṃ ādesā honti. Divā ca ratto ca haranti ye baliṃ (Khu. i, 312)Khuddaka-nikāya · vol. i, p. 312. Bārāṇasiṃ ahu rājā (Khu. v, 380)Khuddaka-nikāya · vol. v, p. 380.

And ‘o’ after “ādi”.
Optionally, the inflection ‘smiṃ’ after “ādi” is substituted by ‘aṃ’ and ‘o’.
Examples
  1. Ādiṃ = ādi + smiṃ (‘smiṃ’ is substituted by ‘aṃ’ (§69); ‘i’ of “ādi” is elided (§83)).
  2. Ādo = ādi + smiṃ (‘smiṃ’ is substituted by ‘o’ (§69); ‘i’ of “ādi” is elided (§83)).

What is the purpose of saying “optionally”? [This sutta does not apply in:] ādismiṃ, ādimhi nāthaṃ namassitvāna (having paid homage to the Lord, in the beginning).

And by taking “ca”, also after other words ‘smiṃ’ is substituted by ‘ā’, ‘o’ and ‘aṃ’.

Examples
  1. Divā = divā + smiṃ (‘smiṃ’ is substituted by ‘ā’ (§69); ‘ā’ of “divā” is elided (§83)).
  2. Ratto = ratti + smiṃ (‘smiṃ’ is substituted by ‘o’ (§69); ‘i’ of “ratti” is elided).
  3. Bārāṇasiṃ = Bārāṇasī + smiṃ (‘smiṃ’ is substituted by ‘aṃ’ (§69); ‘a’ of ‘aṃ’ is elided).

“Divā ca ratto ca haranti ye baliṃ” (those who by day and by night bring offerings). “Bārāṇasiṃ ahu rājā” (there was a king in Vārāṇasī).

Studied
70Kaccāyana Sutta. 30Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Jha-lānam iy’-uvā sare vā (220)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Jha-lānaṃ + iya-uvā + sare + vā = 4 words]

Jha la icc etesaṃ iya uva icc ete ādesā honti vā sare pare yathāsaṅkhyaṃ.

Tiyantaṃ pacchiyāgāre, aggiyāgāre, bhikkhuvāsane nisīdati, puthuvāsane nisīdati.

Sare ti kimatthaṃ? Timalaṃ, tiphalaṃ, ticatukkaṃ, tidaṇḍaṃ, tilokaṃ, tinayanaṃ, tipāsaṃ, tihaṃsaṃ, tibhavaṃ, tikhandhaṃ, tipiṭakaṃ, tivedanaṃ, catuddisaṃ, puthubhūtaṃ.

Vā ti kimatthaṃ? Pañcah’ aṅgehi (Vin. v, 343)Vinaya-piṭaka · vol. v, p. 343, tīhākārehi. Cakkh’ āyatanaṃ (Abhi. iii, 5)Abhidhamma-piṭaka · vol. iii, p. 5.

Vā ti vikappanatthaṃ? Ikārassa ayādeso hoti. Vatthuttayaṃ.

When a vowel follows, optionally, [there are] ‘iya’ and ‘uva’ of ‘jha’ and ‘la’.
Optionally, when a vowel follows, ‘jha’ and ‘la’ are substituted by ‘iya’ and ‘uva’ respectively. i ī — iya u ū — uva
Examples
  1. Tiyantaṃ = ti + antaṃ (‘i’ of ‘ti’ is named ‘jha’ (§58); ‘i’ is substituted by ‘iya’ (§70); ‘a’ of ‘iya’ is elided (§83)).
  2. Bhikkhuvāsane = bhikkhu + āsane (‘u’ of “bhikkhu” is named ‘la’ (§58); ‘u’ is substituted by ‘uva’ (§70); ‘a’ of ‘uva’ is elided (§83)).
  3. The formation of the rest of the examples is similar to the previous ones.

What is the purpose of saying “when a vowel follows”? [This sutta does not apply when a vowel does not follow, such as in] timalaṃ, tiphalaṃ, ticatukkaṃ, tidaṇḍaṃ, tilokaṃ, tinayanaṃ, tipāsaṃ, tihaṃsaṃ, tibhavaṃ, tikhandhaṃ, tipiṭakaṃ, tivedanaṃ, catuddisaṃ, puthubhūtaṃ.

What is the purpose of saying “optionally”? [This sutta does not apply in] pañcah’ aṅgehi, tīhākārehi, cakkh’ āyatanaṃ.

“Vā” is used in the meaning of alternative (vikappana). [By that “vā”] the letter ‘i’ is substituted by ‘aya’. Vatthuttayaṃ = vatthutti + si (by “vā” of this sutta, ‘i’ of ‘ti’ is substituted by ‘aya’; ‘si’ is substituted by ‘aṃ’).

Studied
71Kaccāyana Sutta. 505Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Ya-vakārā ca (221)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Ya-vakārā + ca = 2 words]

Jha-lānaṃ yakāra-vākārādesā honti sare pare yathāsaṅkhyaṃ.

Agyāgāraṃ (Vin. iii, 33)Vinaya-piṭaka · vol. iii, p. 33; cakkh’ āyatanaṃ (Abhi. iii, 5)Abhidhamma-piṭaka · vol. iii, p. 5; svāgataṃ (Khu. v, 300)Khuddaka-nikāya · vol. v, p. 300; te mahāvīra.

Caggahaṇaṃ sampiṇḍanatthaṃ.

And the letters ‘ya’ and ‘va’.
When a vowel follows, ‘jha’ and ‘la’ are substituted by ‘ya’ and ‘va’ respectively.
Examples
  1. Agyāgāraṃ = aggi + āgāraṃ (‘i’ of “aggi” is named ‘jha’ (§58); ‘i’ is substituted by ‘ya’ (§71); ‘a’ of ‘ya’ is elided (§83); ‘g’ of “aggi” is also elided (§41)).
  2. Svāgataṃ = su + āgataṃ (‘u’ is named ‘la’ (§58); ‘u’ is substituted by ‘va’ (§71); ‘a’ of ‘va’ is elided (§83)).
  3. The formation of the rest of the examples is similar to the previous ones.

“Ca” is used in the meaning of collecting (sampiṇḍana).11“Ca” means here sampiṇḍana (collecting), since both this sutta and §70 · Jha-lānam iy’-uvā sare vā — When a vowel follows, optionally, [there are] ‘iya’ and ‘uva’ of ‘jha’ and ‘la’.">§70 have a similar function: in §70 · Jha-lānam iy’-uvā sare vā — When a vowel follows, optionally, [there are] ‘iya’ and ‘uva’ of ‘jha’ and ‘la’.">§70, ‘jha’ and ‘la’ are substituted by ‘iya’ and ‘uva’; in this sutta, by ‘ya’ and ‘va’. The “ca” gathers both operations as a set. Ref. Ven. A. Thitzana.

11“Ca” means here sampiṇḍana (collecting), since both this sutta and §70 have a similar function: in §70, ‘jha’ and ‘la’ are substituted by ‘iya’ and ‘uva’; in this sutta, by ‘ya’ and ‘va’. The “ca” gathers both operations as a set. Ref. Ven. A. Thitzana.

72Kaccāyana Sutta. 185Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Pasaññassa ca (222)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Pa-saññassa + ca = 2 words]

Pasaññassa ca ivaṇṇassa vibhattādese sare pare yakārādeso hoti.

Puthabyā; ratyā (Khu. vi, 315)Khuddaka-nikāya · vol. vi, p. 315; matyā (Khu. vi, 39)Khuddaka-nikāya · vol. vi, p. 39.

  2. The formation of ratyā and matyā is similar to the previous one.

What is the purpose of saying “when a vowel follows”? [This sutta does not apply when a vowel does not follow, such as in] puthaviyaṃ.

73Kaccāyana Sutta. 174Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Gāva se (224)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Go + āva + se = 3 words]

Go icc etassa okārassa āvādeso hoti se vibhattimhi.

Gāvassa.

When ‘sa’ [follows], ‘āva’ of [‘o’ of] “go”.
When the inflection ‘sa’ follows, ‘o’ of “go” is substituted by ‘āva’.
Example
  1. Gāvassa = go + sa (‘o’ of “go” is substituted by ‘āva’ (§73) and ‘s’ is inserted (§61)).

74Kaccāyana Sutta. 169Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Yosu ca (224)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Yosu + ca = 2 words]

Go icc etassa okārassa āvādeso hoti yo icc etesu paresu.

Gāvo gacchanti; gāvo passanti; gāvī gacchanti; gāvī passanti.

Caggahaṇaṃ kimatthaṃ? Nā-smā-smiṃ-suvacanesu āvādeso hoti.

Gāvena, gāvā, gāve, gāvesu.

And when [any of the three]12First plural inflection, second plural inflection and vocative plural. ‘yo’ follow.
When [any of the three] ‘yo’ follow, ‘o’ of “go” is substituted by ‘āva’.
Examples
  1. Gāvo = go + yo (‘o’ of “go” is substituted by ‘āva’ (§74); ‘yo’ is substituted by ‘o’ (“tu” in §205); ‘a’ is elided (§12)).
  2. The formation of the rest of the examples is similar to the previous one.

What is the purpose of taking “ca”? [By taking “ca”, there is the substitution ‘āva’] also when ‘nā’, ‘smā’, ‘smiṃ’ and ‘su’ follow.

Examples
  1. Gāvena = go + nā (‘o’ of “go” is substituted by ‘āva’ by “ca” of this sutta (§74); ‘nā’ is substituted by ‘ena’ (§103); ‘a’ is elided (§12)).
  2. Gāvā = go + smā (‘o’ of “go” is substituted by ‘āva’ by “ca” of this sutta (§74); ‘smā’ is substituted by ‘ā’ (§108); ‘a’ is elided (§12)).
  3. Gāve = go + smiṃ (‘o’ of “go” is substituted by ‘āva’ by “ca” of this sutta (§74); ‘smiṃ’ is substituted by ‘e’ (§108); ‘a’ is elided (§12)).
  4. Gāvesu = go + su (‘o’ of “go” is substituted by ‘āva’ by “ca” of this sutta (§74); ‘a’ is substituted by ‘e’ (§101)).

75Kaccāyana Sutta. 170Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Av’ aṃmhi ca (224)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Ava + aṃ-mhi + ca = 3 words]

Go icc etassa okārassa āva ava icc ete ādesā honti aṃ-mhi vibhattimhi.

Caggahaṇena sādisesesu pubbuttavacanesu go icc etassa okārassa avādeso hoti.

Gāvaṃ, gavaṃ. Gavassa, gavo, gavena, gavā, gave, gavesu.

And when ‘aṃ’ follows, ‘ava’.
When the inflection ‘aṃ’ follows, ‘o’ of “go” is substituted by ‘āva’ and ‘ava’.
Examples
  1. Gāvaṃ = go + aṃ (‘o’ of “go” is substituted by ‘āva’ (§75); ‘a’ is elided (§12)).
  2. Gavaṃ = go + aṃ (‘o’ of “go” is substituted by ‘ava’ (§75); ‘a’ is elided (§12)).

By taking “ca”, when the remaining inflections beginning with ‘sa’ mentioned in the previous [two] suttas follow, ‘o’ of “go” is substituted by ‘ava’.

Examples
  1. Gavassa = go + sa (by “ca” of this sutta, ‘o’ of “go” is substituted by ‘ava’ (§75); ‘s’ is inserted (§61)).
  2. Gavo = go + yo (by “ca” of this sutta, ‘o’ of “go” is substituted by ‘ava’ (§75); ‘yo’ is substituted by ‘o’ (“tu” in §205); ‘a’ is elided (§12)).
  3. Gavena = go + nā (by “ca” of this sutta, ‘o’ of “go” is substituted by ‘ava’ (§75); ‘nā’ is substituted by ‘ena’ (§103); ‘a’ is elided (§12)).
  4. Gavā = go + smā (by “ca” of this sutta, ‘o’ of “go” is substituted by ‘ava’ (§75); ‘smā’ is substituted by ‘ā’ (§108); ‘a’ is elided (§12)).
  5. Gave = go + smiṃ (by “ca” of this sutta, ‘o’ of “go” is substituted by ‘ava’ (§75); ‘smiṃ’ is substituted by ‘e’ (§108); ‘a’ is elided (§12)).
  6. Gavesu = go + su (by “ca” of this sutta, ‘o’ of “go” is substituted by ‘ava’ (§75); ‘a’ is substituted by ‘e’ (§101)).

76Kaccāyana Sutta. 171Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Āvass’ u vā (226)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Āvassa + u + vā = 3 words]

Āva icc etassa gāvādesassa antasarassa ukārādeso hoti vā aṃmhi vibhattimhi.

Gāvuṃ, gāvaṃ.

Āvasse ti kimatthaṃ? Gavaṃ.

Aṃmhi ti kimatthaṃ? Gāvo tiṭṭhanti.

Optionally, ‘u’ of ‘āva’.
Optionally, when the inflection ‘aṃ’ follows, the end vowel of ‘āva’ –which is the substitution of “go”– is substituted by ‘u’.
Examples
  1. Gāvuṃ = go + aṃ (‘o’ of “go” is substituted by ‘āva’ (§73); ‘a’ of ‘āva’ is substituted by ‘u’ (§76); ‘aṃ’ is substituted by ‘ṃ’ (§82)).
  2. Gāvaṃ = no application of this rule.

What is the purpose of saying “of ‘āva’”? [This sutta does not apply in] gavaṃ.

What is the purpose of saying “when ‘aṃ’ follows”? [This sutta does not apply when ‘aṃ’ does not follow, such as in] gāvo tiṭṭhanti.

Studied
77Kaccāyana Sutta. 175Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Tato naṃ aṃ patimh’ ālutte ca samāse (227-8)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Tato + naṃ + aṃ + patimhi + ālutte + ca + samāse = 7 words]

Tato gosaddato naṃvacanassa aṃādeso hoti, go icc etassa okārassa avādeso hoti patimhi pare ālutte ca samāse.

Gavaṃpati (S. iii, 382)Saṃyutta-nikāya · vol. iii, p. 382.

Alutte ti kimatthaṃ? Gopati.

Caggahaṇena asamāse pi naṃvacanassa aṃādeso hoti, go icc etassa okārassa avādeso hoti.

Gavaṃ.

After that [“go”], when ‘pati’ follows in a compound with [the inflection] not elided, ‘aṃ’ of ‘naṃ’.
When there is a compound with [the inflection] not elided (alutta-samāsa), and when ‘pati’ follows, after the word “go” the inflection ‘naṃ’ is substituted by ‘aṃ’ and ‘o’ of “go” is substituted by ‘ava’.
Example
  1. Gavaṃpati = gonaṃ + pati (‘naṃ’ is substituted by ‘aṃ’ (§77); ‘o’ of “go” is substituted by ‘ava’ (§77); ‘a’ of ‘ava’ is elided (§12)).

What is the purpose of saying “in a compound with [the inflection] not elided”? [This sutta does not apply when there is a compound with elision of the inflection, such as in] gopati.

And by taking “ca”, also when there is no compound, ‘naṃ’ is substituted by ‘aṃ’ and ‘o’ of “go” is substituted by ‘ava’.

Example
  1. Gavaṃ = go + naṃ (‘naṃ’ is substituted by ‘aṃ’ (§77); ‘o’ of “go” is substituted by ‘ava’ (§77)).
Studied
78Kaccāyana Sutta. 31Rūpasiddhi Sutta.O sare ca (229)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[O + sare + ca = 3 words]

Go icc etassa okārassa avādeso hoti samāse ca sare pare.

Gavassakaṃ, gaveḷakaṃ, gavājinaṃ.

Caggahaṇena uvaṇṇa icc evam antānaṃ liṅgānaṃ uva-ava-urādesā honti smiṃ-yo icc etesu kvaci.

Bhuvi, pasavo, guravo, caturo (Khu. i, 293)Khuddaka-nikāya · vol. i, p. 293.

Sare ti kimatthaṃ? Godhano, govindho (D. ii, 186)Dīgha-nikāya · vol. ii, p. 186.

And when a vowel follows, ‘o’.
When there is a compound and a vowel follows, ‘o’ of “go” is substituted by ‘ava’.
Example
  1. Gavassakaṃ = go + assakaṃ (‘o’ of “go” is substituted by ‘ava’ (§78); ‘a’ of ‘ava’ is elided (§12)).

And by taking “ca”, when ‘smiṃ’ and ‘yo’ follow, sometimes the bases ending in ‘u’ and ‘ū’ are substituted by ‘uva’, ‘ava’ and ‘ura’.

Examples
  1. Bhuvi = bhū + smiṃ (by “ca” of this sutta, ‘ū’ of “bhū” is substituted by ‘uva’ (§78); by “tato” of §206 ‘smiṃ’ is substituted by ‘i’; ‘a’ of ‘uva’ is elided (§12)).
  2. Pasavo = pasu + yo (by “ca” of this sutta, ‘u’ of “pasu” is substituted by ‘ava’ (§78); ‘yo’ is substituted by ‘o’ (“tu” in §205); ‘a’ of ‘ava’ is elided (§12)).
  3. Caturo = catu + yo (by “ca” of this sutta, ‘u’ is substituted by ‘ura’ (§78); ‘yo’ is substituted by ‘o’ (“tu” in §205); ‘a’ of ‘ura’ is elided (§12)).

What is the purpose of saying “when a vowel follows”? [This sutta does not apply when a vowel does not follow, such as in] godhano, govindho.

Studied
79Kaccāyana Sutta. 46Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Tabbiparītūpapade byañjane ca
[Tabbiparīto + upapade + byañjane + ca = 4 words]

Tassa avasaddassa yadā upapade tiṭṭhamānassa tassa okārassa viparīto hoti byañjane pare.

Uggate sūriye; uggacchati; uggahetvā.

Caggahaṇam avadhāraṇatthaṃ. Avasāne, avakiraṇe, avakirati.

And when [‘ava’] is the preceding member (upapada) and a consonant follows, [there is] reversion of that.
When the word ‘ava’ is the preceding member (upapada) and a consonant follows, ‘o’ of ‘ava’ is reversed [into ‘u’].13‘Ava’ is one of the twenty prefixes (upasagga). The term “viparīta” –change, reversion; transformation– is the name given to the letter ‘o’ which is the transformation of the prefix ‘ava’, and to the letter ‘u’ which is the transformation of the letter ‘o’. E.g., in “ava-gacchati”, he goes down, the prefix ‘ava’ becomes ‘o’ (o-gacchati) and afterwards this becomes ‘u’ (u-gacchati); (Kac. §79 · Tabbiparītūpapade byañjane ca — And when [‘ava’] is the preceding member (*upapada*) and a consonant follows, [there is] reversion of that.">§79, Rū. §45-46, Sad. iii §25-26).
Example
  1. Uggate = ava + gate (‘ava’ is substituted by ‘o’ (§50); then ‘o’ becomes ‘u’ (§79); ‘g’ of “gate” is doubled (§20)).14Note: both changes, ‘ava’ → ‘o’ and ‘o’ → ‘u’, are called viparīta (transformation).

“Ca” is for [delimiting the application of] this rule, [which does not apply in] avasāne, avakiraṇe, avakirati.

13‘Ava’ is one of the twenty prefixes (upasagga). The term “viparīta” –change, reversion; transformation– is the name given to the letter ‘o’ which is the transformation of the prefix ‘ava’, and to the letter ‘u’ which is the transformation of the letter ‘o’. E.g., in “ava-gacchati”, he goes down, the prefix ‘ava’ becomes ‘o’ (o-gacchati) and afterwards this becomes ‘u’ (u-gacchati); (Kac. §79, Rū. §45-46, Sad. iii §25-26).
14Note: both changes, ‘ava’ → ‘o’ and ‘o’ → ‘u’, are called viparīta (transformation).

80Kaccāyana Sutta. 173Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Goṇa naṃmhi vā (231)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Goṇa + naṃmhi + vā = 3 words]

Sabbass’ eva gosaddassa goṇādeso hoti vā naṃmhi vibhattimhi.

Goṇānaṃ sattannaṃ.

Vā ti kimatthaṃ? Gonañ ce taramānānaṃ, ujuṃ gacchati puṅgavo. Sabbā gāvī ujuṃ yanti, nette ujuṃ gate sati.

Yogavibhāgena aññatrā pi goṇādeso hoti.

Goṇabhūtānaṃ.

Optionally, when ‘naṃ’ follows, “goṇa”.
Optionally, when the inflection ‘naṃ’ follows, the whole word “go” is substituted by “goṇa”.
Example
  1. Goṇānaṃ = go + naṃ (“go” is substituted by “goṇa” (§80); ‘a’ of “goṇa” is lengthened (§89)).

What is the purpose of saying “optionally”? [This sutta does not apply in:] “Gonañ ce taramānānaṃ, ujuṃ gacchati puṅgavo. Sabbā gāvī ujuṃ yanti, nette ujuṃ gate sati”. (When the leader of the crossing cattle goes straight, all the cows go straight when the leader goes straight.)

By dividing the sutta, in other contexts there is also the substitution by “goṇa”: goṇabhūtānaṃ.

Studied
81Kaccāyana Sutta. 172Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Su-hi-nāsu ca (231-2)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Su-hi-nāsu + ca = 2 words]

Su hi nā icc etesu sabbassa gosaddassa goṇādeso hoti vā.

Goṇesu, goṇehi, goṇebhi, goṇena.

Vā ti kimatthaṃ? Gosu, gohi, gobhi, gavena.

Caggahaṇena syādisesesu pubbuttaravacanesu pi goṇa-gu-gavayādesā honti. Goṇo, goṇā, goṇaṃ, goṇe, goṇassa, goṇamhā. Goṇamhi, gunnaṃ, gavayehi, gavayebhi.

And when ‘su’, ‘hi’ and ‘nā’ follow.
Optionally, when ‘su’, ‘hi’ and ‘nā’ follow, the whole word “go” is substituted by “goṇa”.
Example
  1. Goṇesu = go + su (“go” is substituted by “goṇa” (§81); ‘a’ of “goṇa” is substituted by ‘e’ (§101)).

What is the purpose of saying “optionally”? [This sutta does not apply in] gosu, gohi, gobhi, gavena.

And by taking “ca”, when the remaining inflections, ‘si’ and others, mentioned before and after, follow, there are also the substitutions by “goṇa”, “gu” and “gavaya”.

Examples
  1. Goṇo = go + si (‘si’ is substituted by ‘o’ (§104); “go” is substituted by “goṇa” (§81); ‘a’ of “goṇa” is elided (§12)).
  2. Gunnaṃ = go + naṃ (“go” is substituted by “gu” (§81); ‘n’ is inserted (§28)).
  3. Gavayehi = go + hi (“go” is substituted by “gavaya” (§81); ‘a’ is substituted by ‘e’ (§108)).
Studied
82Kaccāyana Sutta. 149Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Aṃ-mo niggahitaṃ jha-la-pehi (235)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Aṃ-mo + niggahitaṃ + jha-la-pehi = 3 words]

Aṃvacanassa, makārassa ca jha la pa icc etehi niggahitaṃ hoti.

Aggiṃ, isiṃ, gahapatiṃ, daṇḍiṃ, mahesiṃ, bhikkhuṃ, paṭuṃ, sayambhuṃ, abhibhuṃ, rattiṃ, itthiṃ, vadhuṃ, pulliṅgaṃ, pumbhāvo, puṅkokilo.

Aṃ-mo ti kimatthaṃ? Agginā, pāṇinā, bhikkhunā, rattiyā, itthiyā, vadhuyā.

Jha-la-pehī ti kimatthaṃ? Sukhaṃ, dukkhaṃ.

Pun’ ārambhaggahaṇaṃ vibhāsanivattanatthaṃ. Aggiṃ, paṭuṃ, buddhiṃ, vadhuṃ.

After ‘jha’, ‘la’ and ‘pa’, niggahita [of] ‘aṃ’ and ‘ma’.
After ‘jha’, ‘la’ and ‘pa’, ‘aṃ’ and ‘ma’ become niggahita (ṃ).
Examples
  1. Aggiṃ = aggi + aṃ (‘i’ of “aggi” is named ‘jha’ (§58); ‘aṃ’ becomes ‘ṃ’ (§82)).
  2. Rattiṃ = ratti + aṃ (‘i’ of “ratti” is named ‘pa’ (§59); ‘aṃ’ becomes ‘ṃ’ (§82)).
  3. Pulliṅgaṃ = puma + liṅgaṃ (‘ma’ of “puma” becomes ‘ṃ’ (§82); ‘ṃ’ becomes ‘l’ (§31); ‘l’ is doubled (§28)).

What is the purpose of saying “‘aṃ’ and ‘ma’”? [This sutta does not apply when there is no ‘aṃ’ or ‘ma’, such as in] agginā, pāṇinā, bhikkhunā, rattiyā, itthiyā, vadhuyā.

What is the purpose of saying “after ‘jha’, ‘la’ and ‘pa’”? [This sutta does not apply when there is no ‘jha’, ‘la’ or ‘pa’, such as in] sukhaṃ, dukkhaṃ.

Taking again “jha-la-pehi” is to prevent “vā” from following up to here.15To prevent the application of the optional rule (vibhāsa-nivattana) here. Examples: aggiṃ, paṭuṃ, buddhiṃ, vadhuṃ.

15To prevent the application of the optional rule (vibhāsa-nivattana) here.
Studied
83Kaccāyana Sutta. 67Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Saralopo ’mādesa-paccayādimhi saralope tu pakati (236)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Sara-lopo + aṃ-ādesa-paccaya-ādimhi + saralope + tu + pakati = 5 words]

Saralopo hoti amādesa-paccayādimhi, saralope tu pakati hoti.

Purisaṃ, purise, pāpaṃ, pāpe, pāpiyo, pāpiṭṭho.

Amādesapaccayādimhī ti kimatthaṃ? Appamādo amataṃ padaṃ (Khu. i, 16)Khuddaka-nikāya · vol. i, p. 16.

Saralope ti kimatthaṃ? Purisassa, daṇḍinaṃ.

Tuggahaṇam avadhāraṇatthaṃ? Bhikkhunī, gahapatānī.

Pakatiggahaṇasāmatthena puna sandhibhāvo ca hoti. Seyyo (Khu. i, 29)Khuddaka-nikāya · vol. i, p. 29; seṭṭho (Vin. i, 4)Vinaya-piṭaka · vol. i, p. 4; jeyyo; jeṭṭho (D. ii, 13)Dīgha-nikāya · vol. ii, p. 13.

When ‘aṃ’, a substitution, a suffix, etc., follow, [there is] elision of the vowel; when there is elision of the vowel, [the remaining vowel remains] natural.
When [the inflection] ‘aṃ’, a substitution, a suffix, etc., follow, there is elision of the vowel; and when there is elision of the vowel, [the remaining vowel] remains natural.16“Remains natural” (pakati) means that the vowel does not change.17Note: “Remains natural” (pakati) means that the vowel does not change.
Examples
  1. Purisaṃ = purisa + aṃ (because of ‘aṃ’, there is elision of the vowel ‘a’ of “purisa” (§83); ‘a’ of ‘aṃ’ does not change (§83)).
  2. Pāpiyo = pāpa + iya (‘a’ of “pāpa” is elided (§83); ‘i’ of ‘iya’ does not change (§83)).

What is the purpose of saying “when ‘aṃ’, a substitution, a suffix, etc., [follow]”? [This sutta does not apply when that does not happen, such as in] “Appamādo amataṃ padaṃ”.18Note: Here the initial ‘a’ of “amataṃ” is not the inflection ‘aṃ’, nor a substitution, nor a suffix; therefore this rule does not operate.

What is the purpose of saying “when there is elision of the vowel”? [This sutta does not apply when there is no vowel to elide, such as in] purisassa, daṇḍinaṃ.

‘Tu’ is for preventing the operation of this rule in “bhikkhunī”, “gahapatānī”.

Examples
  1. Bhikkhunī = bhikkhu + inī (here ‘i’ of ‘inī’ is elided (§13)).
  2. Gahapatānī = gahapati + inī (‘i’ of ‘pati’ is substituted by ‘a’ (§91); ‘i’ of ‘inī’ is elided (§13); ‘a’ becomes ‘ā’ (§16)).

Taking again “pakati”, there is also sandhi: seyyo, seṭṭho, jeyyo, jeṭṭho.19The procedure of euphonic combination involves substituting ‘i’ by ‘e’ and doubling ‘y’.

16“Remains natural” (pakati) means that the vowel does not change.
17Note: “Remains natural” (pakati) means that the vowel does not change.
18Note: Here the initial ‘a’ of “amataṃ” is not the inflection ‘aṃ’, nor a substitution, nor a suffix; therefore this rule does not operate.
19The procedure of euphonic combination involves substituting ‘i’ by ‘e’ and doubling ‘y’.

84Kaccāyana Sutta. 144Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Agho rassam ekavacanayosv api ca (237-8)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Agho + rassaṃ + ekavacana-yosu + api + ca = 5 words]

Agho saro rassam āpajjate ekavacana-yo icc etesu.

Itthiṃ, itthiyo, itthiyā. Vadhuṃ, vadhuyo, vadhuyā. Daṇḍiṃ, daṇḍino, daṇḍinā. Sayambhuṃ, sayambhuvo, sayambhunā.

Agho ti kimatthaṃ? Kaññaṃ, kaññāyo, kaññāya.

Ekavacanayosv iti kimatthaṃ? Itthīhi, sayambhūhi.

Caggahaṇam avadhāraṇatthaṃ? Nadiṃ, nadīyo, nadiyā.

Apiggahaṇena na rassam āpajjate. Itthī, bhikkhunī.

And also when the singular [number] and ‘yo’ follow, non-‘gha’ [is shortened].
When the singular [inflection] and ‘yo’ follow, the vowel that is not ‘gha’ is shortened.
Examples
  1. Itthiṃ = itthī + aṃ (‘ī’ of “itthī” is shortened (§84); ‘aṃ’ becomes ‘ṃ’ (§82)).
  2. Itthiyo = itthī + yo (‘ī’ of “itthī” is shortened (§84)).
  3. The formation of the rest of the examples is similar to the previous ones.

What is the purpose of saying “non-‘gha’”? [This sutta does not apply when there is ‘gha’, such as in] kaññaṃ, kaññāyo, kaññāya.

What is the purpose of saying “when the singular [number] and ‘yo’ [follow]”? [This sutta does not apply when that is not the case, such as in] itthīhi, sayambhūhi.

“Ca” is for emphasis.

By taking “api”, there is no shortening.

Examples
  1. Itthī = itthī + si (‘ī’ is not shortened because of “api” in this sutta (§84); ‘si’ is elided (§220)).
Studied
85Kaccāyana Sutta. 150Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Na sismim anapuṃsakāni (239-48)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Na + sismim + anapuṃsakāni = 3 words]

Sismiṃ anapuṃsakāni liṅgāni na rassam āpajjante.

Itthī, bhikkhunī, vadhū, daṇḍī, sayambhū.

Sismiṃ ti kimatthaṃ? Bhoti itthi, bothi vadhu, bho daṇḍi, bho sayambhu.

Anapuṃsakānī ti kimatthaṃ? Sukhakāri dānaṃ, sukhakāri sīlaṃ, sīghayāyi cittaṃ.

When ‘si’ follows, the non-neuters, not [shortened].
When ‘si’ follows, the non-neuter bases are not shortened.
Examples
  1. Itthī = itthī + si (‘ī’ is not shortened; ‘si’ is elided (§220)).

What is the purpose of saying “when ‘si’ [follows]”? [This sutta does not apply when ‘si’ does not follow, such as in] “bhoti itthi”, etc.20These examples do not correspond to the first inflection ‘si’ but to the ‘si’ of the vocative.

Example
  1. Itthi = itthī + si (‘si’ is named ‘gha’ (§57); ‘ī’ is shortened (§245); ‘si’ is elided (§220)).

What is the purpose of saying “non-neuters”? [This sutta does not apply when they are neuter, such as in] “sukhakāri dānaṃ”, etc.

Examples
  1. Sukhakāri = sukhakārī + si (‘si’ is named ‘jha’ (§58); ‘ī’ is shortened by this sutta (§85); ‘si’ is elided (§220)).
20These examples do not correspond to the first inflection ‘si’ but to the ‘si’ of the vocative.

86Kaccāyana Sutta. 227Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Ubhādito nam innaṃ (341)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Ubha-ādito + naṃ + innaṃ = 3 words]

Ubha icc evam ādito saṅkhyāto naṃvacanassa innaṃ hoti.

Ubhinnaṃ, duvinnaṃ.

Ubhādito ti kimatthaṃ? Ubhayesaṃ.

After “ubha” and others, ‘innaṃ’ [of] ‘naṃ’.
After the numerals “ubha” and others, the inflection ‘naṃ’ is substituted by ‘innaṃ’.
Examples
  1. Ubhinnaṃ = ubha + naṃ (‘naṃ’ is substituted by ‘innaṃ’ (§86); ‘a’ of “ubha” is elided (§83)).
  2. Duvinnaṃ = dvi + naṃ (‘naṃ’ is substituted by ‘innaṃ’ (§86); by “ca” (§132) “dvi” is substituted by “duvi”; ‘i’ of “duvi” is elided (§83)).

What is the purpose of saying “after ‘ubha’ and others”? [This sutta does not apply when there is no “ubha” and others, such as in] ubhayesaṃ.21Here the word is “ubhaya”.

21Here the word is “ubhaya”.

87Kaccāyana Sutta. 231Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Iṇṇam-iṇṇannaṃ tīhi saṅkhyāhi (243)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Iṇṇaṃ-iṇṇannaṃ + tīhi + saṅkhyāhi = 3 words]

Naṃvacanassa iṇṇaṃ iṇṇannaṃ icc ete ādesā honti tīhi saṅkhyāhi.

Tiṇṇaṃ, tiṇṇannaṃ.

Tīhī ti kimatthaṃ? Dvinnaṃ.

After the numeral “ti”, ‘iṇṇaṃ’ and ‘iṇṇannaṃ’ [of ‘naṃ’].
After the numeral “ti”, the inflection ‘naṃ’ is substituted by ‘iṇṇaṃ’ and ‘iṇṇannaṃ’.
Examples
  1. Tiṇṇaṃ, tiṇṇannaṃ = ti + naṃ (‘naṃ’ is substituted by ‘iṇṇaṃ’ and ‘iṇṇannaṃ’ (§87); ‘i’ of “ti” is elided (§83)).

What is the purpose of saying “after the numeral ‘ti’”? [This sutta does not apply when there is no ‘ti’, such as in] dvinnaṃ.

Studied
88Kaccāyana Sutta. 147Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Yosu katanikāra-lopesu dīghaṃ (245)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Yosu + kata-nikāra-lopesu + dīghaṃ = 3 words]

Sabbe sarā yosu katanikāra-lopesu dīgham āpajjante.

Aggī, bhikkhū, rattī, yāgū, aṭṭhī, aṭṭhīni, āyū, āyūni, sabbāni, yāni, tāni, kāni, katamāni, etāni, amūni, imāni.

Yosv iti kimatthaṃ? Aggi, bhikkhu, ratti, yāgu, sabbo, yo, so, ko, amuko.

Katanikāralopesv iti kimatthaṃ? Itthiyo, vadhuyo, sayambhuvo.

Pun’ ārambhaggahaṇaṃ kimatthaṃ? Niccadīpanatthaṃ. Aggī, bhikkhū, rattī, yāni, tāni, katamāni.

When ‘yo’ becomes ‘ni’ or is elided, long.
When ‘yo’ becomes ‘ni’ or is elided, all the vowels are lengthened.
Examples
  1. Aggī = aggi + yo (‘yo’ is elided (§118); ‘i’ is lengthened (§88)).
  2. Āyūni = āyu + yo (‘yo’ is substituted by ‘ni’ (§217); ‘u’ is lengthened (§88)).

What is the purpose of saying “when ‘yo’ [follows]”? [This sutta does not apply when there is no ‘yo’, such as in] aggi, bhikkhu, ratti, yāgu, sabbo, yo, so, ko, amuko.

What is the purpose of saying “when it becomes ‘ni’ or is elided”? [This sutta does not apply when it neither becomes ‘ni’ nor is elided, such as in] itthiyo, vadhuyo, sayambhuvo.

What is the purpose of taking this sutta again? To show that it is a fixed operation. Examples: aggī, bhikkhū, rattī, yāni, tāni, katamāni.

Studied
89Kaccāyana Sutta. 87Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Su-naṃ-hisu ca (246)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Su-naṃ-hisu + ca = 2 words]

Su naṃ hi icc etesu sabbe sarā dīgham āpajjante.

Aggīsu, aggīnaṃ, aggīhi; rattīsu, rattīnaṃ, rattīhi; bhikkhūsu, bhikkhūnaṃ, bhikkhūhi. Purisānaṃ.

Etesv iti kimatthaṃ? Agginā, pāṇinā, daṇḍinā.

Caggahaṇam avadhāraṇatthaṃ. Sukhettesu brahmacārisu (A. i, 352)Aṅguttara-nikāya · vol. i, p. 352; dhammam akkhāsi Bhagavā; bhikkhunaṃ datvā sakehi pāṇibhi (Khu. ii, 138)Khuddaka-nikāya · vol. ii, p. 138.

And when ‘su’, ‘naṃ’ and ‘hi’ follow.
When ‘su’, ‘naṃ’ and ‘hi’ follow, all the vowels are lengthened.
Examples
  1. Aggīsu = aggi + su (‘i’ is lengthened (§89)).
  2. The formation of the rest of the examples is similar to the previous one.

What is the purpose of saying “when these follow”? [This sutta does not apply when ‘su’, ‘naṃ’ and ‘hi’ do not follow, such as in] agginā, pāṇinā, daṇḍinā.

“Ca” is for preventing [the application of this rule in the following cases].

Examples
  1. Brahmacārisu = brahmacāri + su (here ‘i’ is not lengthened, by “ca” (§89)).
  2. Bhikkhunaṃ = bhikkhu + naṃ (here ‘u’ is not lengthened).
  3. Pāṇibhi = pāṇi + hi (‘hi’ is substituted by ‘bhi’ (§99); ‘i’ is not lengthened, by “ca” (§89)).

90Kaccāyana Sutta. 252Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Pañcādīnam attaṃ (247)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Pañca-ādīnaṃ + attaṃ = 2 words]

Pañcādīnaṃ saṅkhyānaṃ anto attam āpajjate su naṃ hi icc etesu.

Pañcasu, pañcannaṃ, pañcahi; chasu, channaṃ, chahi; sattasu, sattannaṃ, sattahi; aṭṭhasu, aṭṭhannaṃ, aṭṭhahi; navasu, navannaṃ, navahi; dasasu, dasannaṃ, dasahi.

Pañcādīnamī ti kimatthaṃ? Dvīsu, dvinnaṃ, dvīhi.

Attam iti bhāvaniddeso ubhayassāgamanatthaṃ, anto ukāro attam āpajjate. Catassannaṃ itthīnaṃ. Tissannaṃ vedanānaṃ.

The state of ‘a’ of “pañca” and others.
When ‘su’, ‘naṃ’ and ‘hi’ follow, the end vowel of the numerals “pañca” and others remains ‘a’.
Example
  1. Pañcasu = pañca + su (‘a’ remains ‘a’ (§90)).

What is the purpose of saying “of ‘pañca’ and others”? [This sutta does not apply when there is no “pañca” and others, such as in] dvīsu, dvinnaṃ, dvīhi.

“Attaṃ”, which is an expression that indicates a state (bhāvaniddesa), has the purpose of inserting ‘ssa’ and changing the end ‘u’ into ‘a’.

Example
  1. Catassannaṃ = catu + naṃ (‘ssa’ is inserted; ‘u’ becomes ‘a’ (§90)).
  2. Tissannaṃ = ti + naṃ (‘ssa’ is inserted (§90); ‘n’ is doubled (§28)).22Note: In the sutta it is said “pañcādīnam attaṃ” and not “pañcādīnam a”. “Attaṃ” = state of ‘a’; thus “attaṃ” is called bhāvaniddesa (an expression that indicates a state). The expression that indicates a state has the purpose of inserting ‘ssa’ and changing ‘u’ into ‘a’.
22Note: In the sutta it is said “pañcādīnam attaṃ” and not “pañcādīnam a”. “Attaṃ” = state of ‘a’; thus “attaṃ” is called bhāvaniddesa (an expression that indicates a state). The expression that indicates a state has the purpose of inserting ‘ssa’ and changing ‘u’ into ‘a’.

  1. Gahapatānī = gahapati + inī (‘i’ of “gahapati” becomes ‘a’ (§91); ‘i’ of ‘inī’ is elided (§13); ‘a’ is lengthened (§16)).

What is the purpose of saying “when ‘inī’ follows”? [This sutta does not apply when ‘inī’ does not follow, such as in] gahapati.

92Kaccāyana Sutta. 100Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Ntuss’ anto yosu ca (249)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Ntussa + anto + yosu + ca = 4 words]

Ntupaccayassa anto attam āpajjate su naṃ hi yo icc etesu paresu.

Guṇavantesu, guṇavantānaṃ, guṇavantehi, guṇavantā, guṇavante.

Ntusse ti kimatthaṃ? Isīnaṃ.

Etesv iti kimatthaṃ? Guṇavā.

Caggahaṇena aññesu vacanesu attañ ca hoti. Guṇavantasmiṃ, guṇavantena.

Antaggahaṇena ntupaccayassa anto attam āpajjate, yonañ ca ikāro hoti. Guṇavanti.

And when ‘yo’ [and others] follow, the end of ‘ntu’.
When ‘su’, ‘naṃ’, ‘hi’ and ‘yo’ follow, the end vowel of the suffix ‘ntu’ becomes ‘a’.
Examples
  1. Guṇavantesu = guṇavantu + su (‘u’ of ‘ntu’ becomes ‘a’ (§92); ‘a’ becomes ‘e’ (§89)).
  2. The formation of the rest of the examples is similar to the previous one.

What is the purpose of saying “of ‘ntu’”? [This sutta does not apply when there is no ‘ntu’, such as in] isīnaṃ.

What is the purpose of saying “when these follow”? [This sutta does not apply when ‘su’, ‘naṃ’, ‘hi’ and ‘yo’ do not follow, such as in] guṇavā.

By taking “ca”, when other inflections follow, there is also ‘a’. Examples: guṇavantasmiṃ, guṇavantena.

By taking “anta”, the end vowel of the suffix ‘ntu’ becomes ‘a’, and ‘yo’ becomes ‘i’. Example:

  1. Guṇavanti = guṇavantu + yo (‘u’ of ‘ntu’ becomes ‘a’ by “anta” (§92); ‘yo’ becomes ‘i’ (§92); ‘a’ is elided (§83)).

[Sabbassa + vā + aṃ-sesu = 3 words]

Satimaṃ bhikkhuṃ, satimantaṃ bhikkhuṃ vā. Bandhumaṃ rājānaṃ, bandhumantaṃ rājānaṃ vā (D. ii, 14)Dīgha-nikāya · vol. ii, p. 14. Satimassa bhikkhuno, satimato bhikkhuno vā.   2. Satimassa = satimantu + sa (‘ntu’ becomes ‘a’ (§93); ‘a’ is elided (§83); ‘s’ is inserted (§61)).

What is the purpose of saying “when these follow”? [This sutta does not apply when ‘aṃ’ and ‘sa’ do not follow, such as in] satimā bhikkhu, bandhumā rājā.

96Kaccāyana Sutta. 148Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Yosv akatarasso jho (259)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Yosu + akatarasso + jho = 3 words]

Yosu akatarasso jho attam āpajjate.

Aggayo, munayo, isayo (Khu. ii, 88)Khuddaka-nikāya · vol. ii, p. 88, gahapatayo (Khu. vi, 423)Khuddaka-nikāya · vol. vi, p. 423.

Akatarasso ti kimatthaṃ? Daṇḍino.

Jho ti kimatthaṃ? Rattiyo.

When ‘yo’ follows, ‘jha’ not shortened [becomes ‘a’].
When ‘yo’ follows, ‘jha’, which has not been shortened,23“Akatarasso”, lit., which has not been made short, means that it is naturally short. This sutta applies to the first plural inflection (‘yo’), to the vocative plural (‘yo’) and to the second plural inflection (‘yo’). becomes ‘a’.

  1. Aggayo = aggi + yo (‘i’ is named ‘jha’ (§58) and it has not been shortened; ‘i’ becomes ‘a’ (§96)).

What is the purpose of saying “when ‘yo’ [follows]”? [This sutta does not apply when ‘yo’ does not follow, such as in] aggīsu.

What is the purpose of saying “not shortened”? [This sutta does not apply when it has been shortened, such as in] daṇḍino.

Example

Daṇḍino = daṇḍī + yo (‘ī’ of “daṇḍī” is shortened (§84); therefore this sutta does not operate).

What is the purpose of saying “‘jha’”? [This sutta does not apply when there is no ‘jha’, such as in] rattiyo.

23“Akatarasso”, lit., which has not been made short, means that it is naturally short. This sutta applies to the first plural inflection (‘yo’), to the vocative plural (‘yo’) and to the second plural inflection (‘yo’).

97Kaccāyana Sutta. 156Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Ve-vosu lo ca (260)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta

  1. Bhikkhave = bhikkhu + yo (‘u’ of “bhikkhu” is named ‘la’ (§58); ‘yo’ is substituted by ‘ve’ (§116); ‘u’, which has not been shortened, becomes ‘a’ (§97)).

  3. The formation of the rest of the examples is similar to the previous one.

What is the purpose of saying “not shortened”? [This sutta does not apply when it has been shortened, such as in] sayambhuvo, vessabhuvo, parābhibhuvo.

What is the purpose of saying “when ‘ve’ and ‘vo’ follow”? [This sutta does not apply when ‘ve’ and ‘vo’ do not follow, such as in] hetunā, ketunā, setunā.

“Ca” is for dragging (anukaḍḍhana).

What is the purpose of saying “when ‘ī’ follows”? [This sutta does not apply when ‘ī’ does not follow, such as in] bhikkhunī, rājinī, jālinī, gahapatānī.

Translation: whatever bhikkhu, with the intention of stealing, takes the property of another –whether a quarter of a pāda [coin], or the equivalent of a quarter of a pāda, or more than a quarter of a pāda– that bhikkhu is one who has committed an offence entailing expulsion and can no longer live in communion.

Simhi ti kimatthaṃ? Vaṇṇavantaṃ agandhakaṃ virūḷhapupphaṃ passasi tvaṃ.

In the neuter, ‘aṃ’.
When the inflection ‘si’ follows and the gender is neuter, the whole suffix ‘ntu’ together with the inflection is substituted by ‘aṃ’.
Example
  1. Guṇavaṃ = guṇavantu + si (‘ntu’ together with the inflection ‘si’ is substituted by ‘aṃ’ (§125); ‘a’ is elided (§83)).

What is the purpose of saying “when ‘si’ follows”? [This sutta does not apply when ‘si’ does not follow, such as in] vaṇṇavantaṃ agandhakaṃ virūḷhapupphaṃ passasi tvaṃ.

126Kaccāyana Sutta. 101Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Avaṇṇā ca ge (301-2)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Avaṇṇā + ca + ge = 3 words]

Sabbass’ eva ntupaccayassa savibhattissa aṃ-avaṇṇā ca honti ge pare.

Caggahaṇam anukaḍḍhanatthaṃ.

And when ‘ga’ follows, [there is ‘aṃ’], ‘a’ and ‘ā’.
When ‘ga’ follows, the whole suffix ‘ntu’ together with the inflection is substituted by ‘aṃ’, ‘a’ and ‘ā’.
Example
  1. Guṇavaṃ = guṇavantu + si (‘si’ is named ‘ga’ (§57); ‘ntu’ together with the inflection ‘si’ is substituted by ‘aṃ’ (§126); ‘a’ is elided (§83)).
  2. Guṇava = guṇavantu + si (‘si’ is named ‘ga’ (§57); ‘ntu’ together with the inflection ‘si’ is substituted by ‘a’ (§126); ‘a’ is elided (§83)).
  3. Guṇavā = guṇavantu + si (‘si’ is named ‘ga’ (§57); ‘ntu’ together with the inflection ‘si’ is substituted by ‘ā’ (§126); ‘a’ is elided (§83)).

“Ca” is for dragging.

  1. Guṇavato = guṇavantu + sa (‘ntu’ together with the inflection ‘sa’ is substituted by ‘to’ (§127)).
  2. Guṇavati = guṇavantu + smiṃ (‘ntu’ together with the inflection ‘smiṃ’ is substituted by ‘ti’ (§127)).
  3. Guṇavatā = guṇavantu + nā (‘ntu’ together with the inflection ‘nā’ is substituted by ‘tā’ (§127)).
  4. Satimato = satimantu + sa (‘ntu’ together with the inflection ‘sa’ is substituted by ‘to’ (§127)).
  5. Satimati = satimantu + smiṃ (‘ntu’ together with the inflection ‘smiṃ’ is substituted by ‘ti’ (§127)).
  6. Satimatā = satimantu + nā (‘ntu’ together with the inflection ‘nā’ is substituted by ‘tā’ (§127)).

What is the purpose of saying “when these follow”? [This sutta does not apply when these do not follow, such as in] guṇavā, satimā.

133Kaccāyana Sutta. 230Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Ti-catunnaṃ tisso catasso tayo cattāro tīṇi cattāri (311)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Ti-catunnaṃ + tisso-catasso-tayo-cattāro-tīṇi-cattāri = 2 words]

Tisso vedanā (D. iii, 181)Dīgha-nikāya · vol. iii, p. 181; catasso disā; tayo janā (Khu. v, 196)Khuddaka-nikāya · vol. v, p. 196; cattāro purisā; tīṇi āyatanāni; cattāri ariyasaccāni (Khu. i, 3)Khuddaka-nikāya · vol. i, p. 3.

“Tisso”, “catasso”, “tayo”, “cattāro”, “tīṇi”, “cattāri” [of] “ti” and “catu”.
When ‘yo’ follows, the numerals “ti” and “catu”, which are feminine, masculine and neuter, together with the inflections are substituted by “tisso”, “catasso”, “tayo”, “cattāro”, “tīṇi” and “cattāri” respectively.
Example
  1. Tisso = ti + yo (“ti”, which is feminine, together with the inflection ‘yo’ is substituted by “tisso” (§133)).
  2. Catasso = catu + yo (“catu”, which is feminine, together with the inflection ‘yo’ is substituted by “catasso” (§133)).
  3. Tayo = ti + yo (“ti”, which is masculine, together with the inflection ‘yo’ is substituted by “tayo” (§133)).
  4. Cattāro = catu + yo (“catu”, which is masculine, together with the inflection ‘yo’ is substituted by “cattāro” (§133)).
  5. Tīṇi = ti + yo (“ti”, which is neuter, together with the inflection ‘yo’ is substituted by “tīṇi” (§133)).
  6. Cattāri = catu + yo (“catu”, which is neuter, together with the inflection ‘yo’ is substituted by “cattāri” (§133)).

What is the purpose of saying “when ‘yo’ follows”? [This sutta does not apply when ‘yo’ does not follow, such as in] tīsu, catūsu.

Caggahaṇam anukaḍḍhanatthaṃ.

And occasionally “tavaṃ” and “mamaṃ”.
Occasionally, when the inflection ‘aṃ’ follows, the whole word “tumha” together with the inflection is substituted by “tavaṃ”, and the whole word “amha” together with the inflection is substituted by “mamaṃ”.
Examples
  1. Tavaṃ = tumha + aṃ (“tumha” together with the inflection ‘aṃ’ is substituted by “tavaṃ” (§144)).
  2. Mamaṃ = amha + aṃ (“amha” together with the inflection ‘aṃ’ is substituted by “mamaṃ” (§144)).

What is the purpose of saying “occasionally”? [To exclude the cases in which this rule does not apply, such as in] taṃ, maṃ passati.

“Ca” is for dragging.32To bring the word “aṃmhi” from the previous sutta.

Pahāya vo bhikkhave gamissāmi (Khu. iv, 265)Khuddaka-nikāya · vol. iv, p. 265; mā no ajja vikantiṃsu (Khu. vi, 93)Khuddaka-nikāya · vol. vi, p. 93 rañño sūdā mahānase. Evaṃ dutiyatthe.

Navā ti kimatthaṃ? Eso amhākaṃ satthā.

After a word, when the second, fourth and sixth [inflections] follow, “vo” and “no”.
Occasionally, when the second, fourth and sixth inflections in the plural follow, the whole words “tumha” and “amha”, when they come after a word, together with the inflections, are substituted by “vo” and “no” respectively.33“Vo” and “no” cannot come at the beginning of a sentence.
Examples in the sense of the second [inflection]
  1. Vo = tumha + yo (“tumha” together with the second plural inflection ‘yo’ is substituted by “vo” (§147)).
  2. No = amha + yo (“amha” together with the second plural inflection ‘yo’ is substituted by “no” (§147)).

“Pahāya vo bhikkhave gamissāmi” (having left you, O bhikkhus, I will go).

“Mā no ajja vikantiṃsu rañño sūdā mahānase” (may the king's cooks not cut us up today in the royal kitchen).

Examples in the sense of the fourth [inflection]
  1. Vo = tumha + naṃ (“tumha” together with the fourth plural inflection ‘naṃ’ is substituted by “vo” (§147)).
  2. No = amha + naṃ (“amha” together with the fourth plural inflection ‘naṃ’ is substituted by “no” (§147)).

“Dhammaṃ vo bhikkhave desessāmi” (O bhikkhus, I will teach you the Dhamma).

“Saṃvibhajetha no rajjena” (share the kingdom with us).

Examples in the sense of the sixth [inflection]
  1. Vo = tumha + naṃ (“tumha” together with the sixth plural inflection ‘naṃ’ is substituted by “vo” (§147)).
  2. No = amha + naṃ (“amha” together with the sixth plural inflection ‘naṃ’ is substituted by “no” (§147)).

“Tuṭṭho ’smi vo bhikkhave pakatiyā” (O bhikkhus, I am satisfied with your nature).

“Satthā no Bhagavā anuppatto” (the Blessed One, our Teacher, has arrived).

What is the purpose of saying “occasionally”? [This sutta does not always apply, such as in] eso amhākaṃ satthā.

What is the purpose of saying “of ‘tumha’ and ‘amha’”? [This sutta does not apply when there is no “tumha” or “amha”, such as in] ete isayo passasi.

What is the purpose of saying “after a word”? [This sutta does not apply when they do not come after a word, such as in] tumhākaṃ satthā.

What is the purpose of saying “when the second, fourth and sixth [inflections] follow”? [This sutta does not apply when these inflections do not follow, such as in] gacchatha tumhe.

And when [those inflections] follow in the singular, “te” and “me”.
When the fourth and sixth inflections in the singular follow, the whole words “tumha” and “amha”, when they come after a word, together with the inflections, are substituted by “te” and “me” respectively.

  1. Te = tumha + sa (“tumha” together with the fourth singular inflection ‘sa’ is substituted by “te” (§148)).
  2. Me = amha + sa (“amha” together with the fourth singular inflection ‘sa’ is substituted by “me” (§148)).

“Dadāhi me gāmavaraṃ” (give me a village as a reward).

“Ayaṃ me putto” (this is my son).

What is the purpose of saying “after a word”? [This sutta does not apply when they do not come after a word, such as in] tava ñāti, mama ñāti.

“Passeyya taṃ vassasataṃ arogaṃ” (may you see him in health for a hundred years).

“So maṃ bravīti” (he speaks to me).

152Kaccāyana Sutta. 136Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Pumantass’ ā simhi (331-2)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta

[Hi-vibhattimhi + ca = 2 words]

Puna vibhattiggahaṇaṃ kimatthaṃ? Savibhattiggahaṇa-nivattanatthaṃ. Pumānehi.

Caggahaṇena maghava yuva icc evamādīnam antassa āna-ādeso hoti si yo aṃ yo icc etesu vibhattīsu. Puma-kamma-thāmantassa c’ ukāro hoti sa-smāsu vibhattīsu. Maghavāno. Maghavānā, maghavānaṃ, maghavāne. Yuvāno, yuvānā, yuvānaṃ, yuvāne; pumuno, pumunā. Kammuno, kammunā. Thāmuno, thāmunā.

  1. Pumānehi = puma + hi (‘a’ of “puma” is substituted by ‘āne’ (§157)).

What is the purpose of taking “vibhatti” again? To prevent the inclusion of “savibhatti”34This means that, unlike the previous suttas, in this sutta only the end vowel of “puma” is substituted. in this sutta. Example: pumānehi.

By taking “ca”, when the inflections ‘si’, ‘yo’, ‘aṃ’ and ‘yo’ follow, the end vowel of “maghava”, “yuva”, etc., is substituted by ‘āna’. And when the inflections ‘sa’ and ‘smā’ follow, the [end] vowel of “puma”, “kamma” and “thāma” is substituted by the letter ‘u’.

Examples
  1. Maghavāno = maghava + si (by “ca”, ‘a’ of “maghava” is substituted by ‘āna’ (§157); ‘si’ is substituted by ‘o’ (§104); ‘a’ of ‘āna’ is elided (§83)).
  2. Maghavānā = maghava + yo (by “ca”, ‘a’ of “maghava” is substituted by ‘āna’ (§157); ‘yo’ is substituted by ‘ā’ (§107); ‘a’ of ‘āna’ is elided (§83)).
  3. Maghavānaṃ = maghava + aṃ (by “ca”, ‘a’ of “maghava” is substituted by ‘āna’ (§157); ‘a’ of ‘āna’ is elided (§83)).
  4. Maghavāne = maghava + yo (by “ca”, ‘a’ of “maghava” is substituted by ‘āna’ (§157); ‘yo’ is substituted by ‘e’ (§107); ‘a’ of ‘āna’ is elided (§83)).
  5. The formation of yuvāno, yuvānā, yuvānaṃ, yuvāne is similar to the previous one.
  6. Pumuno = puma + sa (by “ca”, ‘a’ of “puma” is substituted by ‘u’ (§157); ‘u’ is named ‘la’ (§58); ‘sa’ is substituted by ‘no’ (§117)).
  7. Pumunā = puma + smā (by “ca”, ‘a’ of “puma” is substituted by ‘u’ (§157); ‘u’ is named ‘la’ (§58); ‘smā’ is substituted by ‘nā’ (§215)).
  8. The formation of kammuno, kammunā, thāmuno, thāmunā is similar to the previous one.
34This means that, unlike the previous suttas, in this sutta only the end vowel of “puma” is substituted.

Tumhākaṃ passāmi, tumhe passāmi vā. Amhākaṃ passasi, amhe passasi vā.

Yo ti kimatthaṃ? Tumhehi, amhehi.

Appaṭhamo ti kimatthaṃ? Gacchatha tumhe, gacchāma mayaṃ.

Vā ti vikappanatthena yonaṃ aṃ ānaṃ honti. Tumhaṃ, tumhānaṃ. Amhaṃ, amhānaṃ.

Optionally, ‘yo’ which is not the first.
Optionally, after [the bases] “tumha” and “amha”, ‘yo’, which is not the first [inflection], becomes ‘ākaṃ’.
Examples
  1. Tumhākaṃ = tumha + yo (‘yo’ is substituted by ‘ākaṃ’ (§162); ‘a’ of “tumha” is elided (§83)).
  2. Amhākaṃ = amha + yo (‘yo’ is substituted by ‘ākaṃ’ (§162); ‘a’ of “amha” is elided (§83)).

What is the purpose of saying “yo”? [This sutta does not apply when there is no ‘yo’, such as in:] Tumhehi, amhehi.

What is the purpose of saying “which is not the first [inflection]”? [This sutta does not apply when it is the first inflection, such as in:] Gacchatha tumhe, gacchāma mayaṃ.

By ‘vā’, as an alternative, ‘yo’ is substituted by ‘aṃ’ or ‘ānaṃ’.

Examples
  1. Tumhaṃ = tumha + yo (‘yo’ is substituted by ‘aṃ’ (§162); ‘a’ is elided (§83)).
  2. Tumhānaṃ = tumha + yo (‘yo’ is substituted by ‘ānaṃ’ (§162); ‘a’ is elided (§83)).

Optionally, after [the bases] “tumha” and “amha”, the inflection ‘sa’ is substituted by ‘aṃ’.
Example
  1. Tumhaṃ = tumha + sa (‘sa’ is substituted by ‘aṃ’ (§163); ‘a’ is elided (§83)).

What is the purpose of saying “of ‘sa’”? [This sutta does not apply when there is no ‘sa’, such as in:] Tumhesu, amhesu.

164Kaccāyana Sutta. 200Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Sabbanāmakārat’ e paṭhamo (347)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta

Sabbe, ye, te, ke, tumhe, amhe, ime.

Sabbanāmā ti kimatthaṃ? Devā, asurā, nāgā, gandhabbā, manussā.

Yo ti kimatthaṃ? Sabbo, yo, so, ko, ayaṃ.

Paṭhamaggahaṇaṃ uttarasuttatthaṃ.

After the letter ‘a’ of the pronouns, the first [is substituted by] ‘e’.
After the letter ‘a’ of all the pronouns, the first [inflection] ‘yo’ becomes ‘e’.

  1. Sabbe = sabba + yo (‘yo’ becomes ‘e’ (§164); ‘a’ is elided (§83)).
  2. Ye = ya + yo (‘yo’ becomes ‘e’ (§164); ‘a’ is elided (§83)).
  3. Te = ta + yo (‘yo’ is substituted by ‘e’ (§164); ‘a’ is elided (§83)).

What is the purpose of saying “all the pronouns”? [This sutta does not apply when there are no pronouns, such as in:] Devā, asurā, nāgā, gandhabbā, manussā.

What is the purpose of saying “after the letter ‘a’”? [This sutta does not apply when there is no ‘a’, such as in:] Amū purisā tiṭṭhanti.

What is the purpose of saying “[the first inflection] ‘yo’”? [This sutta does not apply when there is no ‘yo’, such as in:] Sabbo, yo, so, ko, ayaṃ.

The taking of “paṭhama” is for the purpose of the following sutta.

  2. Pitari = pitu + smiṃ (‘u’ of “pitu” becomes ‘āra’ (§200); ‘smiṃ’ is substituted by ‘i’ (§206); ‘ā’ of “āra” is shortened (§208); ‘a’ is elided (§83)).

  4. Dhītari = dhītu + smiṃ (‘u’ of “dhītu” becomes ‘āra’ (§200); ‘smiṃ’ is substituted by ‘i’ (§206); ‘ā’ of “āra” is shortened (§208); ‘a’ is elided (§83)).
  5. Kattari = kattu + smiṃ (‘u’ of “kattu” becomes ‘āra’ (§200); ‘smiṃ’ is substituted by ‘i’ (§206); ‘ā’ of “āra” is shortened (§208); ‘a’ is elided (§83)).
  6. Vattari = vattu + smiṃ (‘u’ of “vattu” becomes ‘āra’ (§200); ‘smiṃ’ is substituted by ‘i’ (§206); ‘ā’ of “āra” is shortened (§208); ‘a’ is elided (§83)).

209Kaccāyana Sutta. 168Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Pitādīnam asimhi (425)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Pitu-ādīnaṃ + asimhi = 2 words]

Pitādīnam ārādeso rassam āpajjate asimhi vibhattimhi.

Pitarā, mātarā, bhātarā, dhītarā, pitaro, mātaro, bhātaro, dhītaro.

Asimhiggahaṇam tomhi pare ikārādesañāpanatthaṃ. Mātito (D. i, 106)Dīgha-nikāya · vol. i, p. 106, pitito (D. i, 106)Dīgha-nikāya · vol. i, p. 106, bhātito, duhitito.

When [an inflection] other than ‘si’ follows, of “pitu”, etc.

Examples
  1. Pitarā = pitu + nā (‘u’ of “pitu” becomes ‘āra’ (§200); ‘nā’ is substituted by ‘ā’ (§207); ‘ā’ of “āra” is shortened (§209); ‘a’ is elided (§83)).
  2. Mātarā = mātu + nā (‘u’ of “mātu” becomes ‘āra’ (§200); ‘nā’ is substituted by ‘ā’ (§207); ‘ā’ of “āra” is shortened (§209); ‘a’ is elided (§83)).
  3. Bhātarā = bhātu + nā (‘u’ of “bhātu” becomes ‘āra’ (§200); ‘nā’ is substituted by ‘ā’ (§207); ‘ā’ of “āra” is shortened (§209); ‘a’ is elided (§83)).
  4. Dhītarā = dhītu + nā (‘u’ of “dhītu” becomes ‘āra’ (§200); ‘nā’ is substituted by ‘ā’ (§207); ‘ā’ of “āra” is shortened (§209); ‘a’ is elided (§83)).
  5. Pitaro = pitu + yo (‘u’ of “pitu” becomes ‘āra’ (§200); ‘yo’ is substituted by ‘o’ (§205); ‘ā’ of “āra” is shortened (§209); ‘a’ is elided (§83)).
  6. Mātaro = mātu + yo (‘u’ of “mātu” becomes ‘āra’ (§200); ‘yo’ is substituted by ‘o’ (§205); ‘ā’ of “āra” is shortened (§209); ‘a’ is elided (§83)).
  7. Bhātaro = bhātu + yo (‘u’ of “bhātu” becomes ‘āra’ (§200); ‘yo’ is substituted by ‘o’ (§205); ‘ā’ of “āra” is shortened (§209); ‘a’ is elided (§83)).
  8. Dhītaro = dhītu + yo (‘u’ of “dhītu” becomes ‘āra’ (§200); ‘yo’ is substituted by ‘o’ (§205); ‘ā’ of “āra” is shortened (§209); ‘a’ is elided (§83)).

The taking of “asimhi” is for showing the substitution ‘i’ when ‘to’ follows.

Examples
  1. Mātito = mātu + to (‘u’ of “mātu” is substituted by ‘i’ (“asimhi” in §209)).
  2. Pitito = pitu + to (‘u’ of “pitu” is substituted by ‘i’ (“asimhi” in §209)).
  3. Bhātito = bhātu + to (‘u’ of “bhātu” is substituted by ‘i’ (“asimhi” in §209)).
  4. Duhitito = duhitu + to (‘u’ of “duhitu” is substituted by ‘i’ (“asimhi” in §209)).

210Kaccāyana Sutta. 239Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Tayā-tayīnaṃ takāro tvattaṃ vā (435)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Tayā-tayīnaṃ + takāro + tvattaṃ + vā = 4 words]

Tayā tayi icc etesaṃ takāro tvattam āpajjate vā.

Tvayā, tayā; tvayi, tayi.

Etesam iti kimatthaṃ? Tuvaṃ, tavaṃ.

Optionally, the letter ‘ta’ of “tayā” and “tayi” [becomes] ‘tva’.
Optionally, the letter ‘ta’ of [the substitutions] “tayā” and “tayi” becomes ‘tva’.

  1. Tvayā = tumha + nā (“tumha” together with the inflection is substituted by “tayā” (§145); ‘ta’ becomes ‘tva’ (§210)).

  3. Tvayi = tumha + smiṃ (“tumha” together with the inflection is substituted by “tayi” (§139); ‘ta’ becomes ‘tva’ (§210)).
  4. Tayi = tumha + smiṃ (“tumha” together with the inflection is substituted by “tayi” (§139)).

What is the purpose of saying “of these [substitutions]”? [This sutta does not apply when there is no “tayā” or “tayi”, such as in:] tuvaṃ, tavaṃ.

211Kaccāyana Sutta. 126Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Attanto hismim anattaṃ (439)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Atta-anto + hismiṃ + anattaṃ = 3 words]

Tassa attano anto anattam āpajjate himhi vibhattimhi.

Attanehi, attanebhi.

Attanto ti kimatthaṃ? Rājehi, rājebhi.

Hismin iti kimatthaṃ? Attano.

Anattam iti bhāvaniddesena attasaddassa sakādeso hoti sabbāsu vibhattīsu. Sako, sakā, sakaṃ, sake.

When ‘hi’ follows, [there is] ‘ana’ of the end of “atta”.

  1. Attanehi = atta + hi (‘a’ of “atta” becomes ‘ana’ (§211); ‘a’ is substituted by ‘e’ (§101)).
  2. Attanebhi = atta + hi (‘a’ of “atta” becomes ‘ana’ (§211); ‘a’ is substituted by ‘e’ (§101); ‘hi’ is substituted by ‘bhi’ (§99)).

What is the purpose of saying “when ‘hi’ follows”? [This sutta does not apply when ‘hi’ does not follow, such as in:] attano.47Attanā (Sī).

215Kaccāyana Sutta. 141Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Jha-lato ca (442)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta49Caggahaṇaṃ kvaci nivattanatthaṃ (Rū.), caggahaṇaṃ tadanukaḍḍhanatthaṃ (Nyā.) (The taking of “ca” is for excluding “kvaci” (Rū.); the taking of “ca” is for the dragging of that (Nyā.)).

216Kaccāyana Sutta. 180Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Gha-pato smiṃ yaṃ vā (443)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Gha-pato + smiṃ + yaṃ + vā = 4 words]

Kaññāyaṃ, kaññāya; rattiyaṃ, rattiyā; itthiyaṃ, itthiyā; yāguyaṃ, yāguyā; vadhuyaṃ, vadhuyā.

  5. Itthiyaṃ = itthī + smiṃ (‘ī’ is named ‘pa’ (§59); ‘ī’ is shortened (§84); ‘smiṃ’ is substituted by ‘yaṃ’ (§216)).

  7. Yāguyaṃ = yāgu + smiṃ (‘u’ is named ‘pa’ (§59); ‘smiṃ’ is substituted by ‘yaṃ’ (§216)).

217Kaccāyana Sutta. 199Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Yonaṃ ni napuṃsakehi (444)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Yonaṃ + ni + napuṃsakehi = 3 words]

Sabbesaṃ yonaṃ ni hoti vā napuṃsakehi liṅgehi.

Aṭṭhīni, aṭṭhī; āyūni, āyū. Napuṃsakehī ti kimatthaṃ? Itthiyo.

  1. Aṭṭhīni = aṭṭhi + yo (‘yo’ is substituted by ‘ni’ (§217); ‘i’ is lengthened (§88)).
  2. Aṭṭhī = aṭṭhi + yo (‘yo’ is elided (§118); ‘i’ is lengthened (§88)).
  3. Āyūni = āyu + yo (‘yo’ is substituted by ‘ni’ (§217); ‘u’ is lengthened (§88)).
  4. Āyū = āyu + yo (‘yo’ is elided (§118); ‘u’ is lengthened (§88)).

What is the purpose of saying “after the neuter [bases]”? [This sutta does not apply when there are no neuter bases, such as in:] itthiyo.

218Kaccāyana Sutta. 196Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Ato niccaṃ (445)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Ato + niccaṃ = 2 words]

Akārantehi napuṃsakaliṅgehi yonaṃ ni hoti niccaṃ.

Yāni, yāni; tāni, tāni; kāni, kāni; bhayāni, bhayāni; rūpāni, rūpāni.

  4. Bhayāni = bhaya + yo (‘yo’ is substituted by ‘ni’ (§218); ‘a’ is lengthened (§88)).

  3. Taṃ = ta + si (‘si’ is substituted by ‘aṃ’ (§219); ‘a’ is elided (§83)).
  4. Kaṃ = ka + si (‘si’ is substituted by ‘aṃ’ (§219); ‘a’ is elided (§83)).

220Kaccāyana Sutta. 74Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Sesato lopaṃ ga si pi (447)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Sesato + lopaṃ + gasi + api = 4 words]

Tato niddiṭṭhehi liṅgehi sesato ga si icc ete lopam āpajjante.

Bhoti itthi, sā itthī. Bho daṇḍi, so daṇḍī. Bho sattha, so satthā. Bho rāja, so rājā.

Sesato ti kimatthaṃ? Puriso gacchati.

Ga-sī ti kimatthaṃ? Itthiyā; satthussa.

After the remaining ones, ‘ga’ and ‘si’ are also elided.
After the remaining bases that have been shown,50Those shown by the suttas “Si ’ṃ” (§219 · Si ’ṃ — ‘Si’ [becomes] ‘aṃ’.">§219), “S’ o” (§104 · S’ o — ‘Si’ [becomes] ‘o’.">§104), “Sy ā ca” (§189 · Sy ā ca — And ‘si’ [becomes] ‘ā’.">§189), “Sakhato gass’ e vā” (§113 · Sakhato gass’ e vā — Optionally, ‘e’ of ‘ga’ after “sakha”.">§113) and “Ghat’ e ca” (§114 · Ghat’ e ca — And ‘e’ after ‘gha’.">§114) are called here “sesa” [remaining]. ‘ga’ and ‘si’ are elided.
Examples
  1. Itthi = itthī + si (‘si’ is named ‘ga’ (§57); ‘ī’ is named ‘pa’ (§59); ‘ī’ is shortened (§245); ‘ga’ is elided (§220)).
  2. Itthī = itthī + si (‘si’ is elided (§220)).
  3. Daṇḍi = daṇḍī + si (‘si’ is named ‘ga’ (§57); ‘ī’ is named ‘jha’ (§58); ‘ī’ is shortened (§245); ‘ga’ is elided (§220)).
  4. Daṇḍī = daṇḍī + si (‘si’ is elided (§220)).
  5. Sattha = satthu + si (‘si’ is named ‘ga’ (§57); ‘u’ of “satthu” becomes ‘ā’ (§244); ‘ā’ is shortened (§246); ‘ga’ is elided (§220)).
  6. Satthā = satthu + si (‘u’ of “satthu” becomes ‘ā’ (§199); ‘si’ is elided (§199)).
  7. Rāja = rāja + si (‘si’ is named ‘ga’ (§57); ‘a’ becomes ‘ā’ (§244); ‘ā’ is shortened (§246); ‘ga’ is elided (§220)).
  8. Rājā = rāja + si (‘si’ is substituted by ‘ā’ (§189); ‘a’ is elided (§83)).

What is the purpose of saying “after the remaining ones”? [This sutta does not apply when there are no remaining bases, such as in:] Puriso gacchati.

What is the purpose of saying “‘ga’ and ‘si’”? [This sutta does not apply when ‘ga’ or ‘si’ do not follow, such as in:] itthiyā; satthussa.

50Those shown by the suttas “Si ’ṃ” (§219), “S’ o” (§104), “Sy ā ca” (§189), “Sakhato gass’ e vā” (§113) and “Ghat’ e ca” (§114) are called here “sesa” [remaining].

221Kaccāyana Sutta. 282Rūpasiddhi Sutta.Sabbāsam āvuso-’pasagga-nipātādīhi ca (448)Saddanīti-Suttamālā Sutta
[Sabbāsaṃ + āvuso-upasagga-nipāta-ādīhi + ca = 3 words]

Sabbāsaṃ vibhattīnaṃ ekavacanabahuvacanānaṃ paṭhamā-dutiyā-tatiyā-catutthī-pañcamī-chaṭṭhī-sattamīnaṃ lopo hoti āvuso upasagga nipāta icc evamādīhi ca.

Tvaṃ pan’ āvuso (Vin. ii, 1)Vinaya-piṭaka · vol. ii, p. 1; tumhe pan’ āvuso (Vin. ii, 161)Vinaya-piṭaka · vol. ii, p. 161; padaso dhammaṃ vāceyya (Vin. ii, 25)Vinaya-piṭaka · vol. ii, p. 25; vihāraṃ sve upagaccheyya. Pa, parā, ni, nī, u, du, saṃ, vi, ava, anu, pari, adhi, abhi, pati, su, ā, ati, api, apa, upa. Pahāro, parābhavo, nihāro, nīhāro, uhāro, duhāro, saṃhāro, vihāro, avahāro, anuhāro, parihāro, adhihāro, abhihāro, patihāro, suhāro, āhāro, atihāro, apihāro, apahāro, upahāro. Evaṃ vīsati upasaggehi ca, yathā, tathā, evaṃ, khalu, kho, tatra, atho, atha, hi, tu, ca, vā, vo, haṃ, ahaṃ, alaṃ, eva, ho, aho, he, ahe, re, are. Evamādīhi nipātehi ca yojetabbāni.

Caggahaṇam avadhāraṇatthaṃ.

And after “āvuso”, the prefixes, the particles, etc., [there is elision] of all.
After “āvuso”, the prefixes, the particles, etc., all the inflections, singular and plural, are elided, namely: first, second, third, fourth, fifth, sixth and seventh.
Examples
  1. Tvaṃ pan’ āvuso (and you, friend?)
  2. Tumhe pan’ āvuso (and you, friends?)
  3. Padaso dhammaṃ vāceyya (he should have the Dhamma recited word by word)
  4. Vihāraṃ sve upagaccheyya (he should approach the monastery tomorrow).
  5. Āvuso = āvuso + si (‘si’ is elided (§221)).51Note: This rule is to be employed after the twenty prefixes, ‘pa’, etc., and the particles, ‘yathā’, etc.

The twenty prefixes are the following: pa, parā, ni, nī, u, du, saṃ, vi, ava, anu, pari, adhi, abhi, pati, su, ā, ati, api, apa, upa. [Examples:] Pahāro, parābhavo, nihāro, nīhāro, uhāro, duhāro, saṃhāro, vihāro, avahāro, anuhāro, parihāro, adhihāro, abhihāro, patihāro, suhāro, āhāro, atihāro, apihāro, apahāro, upahāro.

Thus with the twenty prefixes; and they should be employed [likewise] with the particles yathā, tathā, evaṃ, khalu, kho, tatra, atho, atha, hi, tu, ca, vā, vo, haṃ, ahaṃ, alaṃ, eva, ho, aho, he, ahe, re, are, etc.

The taking of “ca” is for restricting [the scope of this sutta].

51Note: This rule is to be employed after the twenty prefixes, ‘pa’, etc., and the particles, ‘yathā’, etc.
